# Appendix DW - CORRECTION to DV: two-lane roads DO fit (span 2700, spare 100) — I held pitch fixed and ignored best_straight; stop sign placed and relocation proven (2026-09-06, ~16:04 CDT)
**CORRECTION to Appendix DV, written 6 minutes earlier.** Evan asked whether
two-lane roads (one lane each direction) are possible. They are. DV says they
are not, and that claim drove Evan's choice of option 2.

## The wrong claim and the right number

DV (and `cad/marking_specs.py`, now corrected) said:

> Two lanes would be 620 mm. Span goes 2690 -> 3000 mm against 2800 mm usable:
> **the 3x3 grid would not fit at all.**

Real output of `cad/track_layout_v2.py --car-width 0.310` (lane = 2 x 310 =
620 mm road):

    lane width      620 mm
    street pitch    1040 mm  (straight between corners 40 mm)
    span            2700 mm of 2800 usable -> 100 mm SPARE
    driven route    figure-8 through the centre intersection, 7.03 m
    track_layout_v2 self_check: PASS

**Two lanes fit, with the full 100 mm reserve intact.**

## Root cause of the error

I computed the two-lane span by adding the extra 310 mm of road to the existing
2690 mm span **while holding pitch fixed**. Pitch is not fixed. `best_straight`
shrinks the straight run (190 -> 40 mm) to protect `SPARE_MIN` — which is
exactly the self-correcting behaviour I added to that file in **Appendix DS,
one turn earlier the same day**, and then described in DS as "the layout now
self-corrects: a future width increase shrinks the straight instead of failing
the check." I wrote the mechanism and then reasoned as though it did not exist.

**The generator was authoritative the whole time and I did not run it.** DS's
own closing line — "the runnable, self-checking generator is the authority" —
is the rule I broke.

## What two lanes actually cost

| | 1 lane (BUILT) | 2 lanes |
|---|---|---|
| road width | 310 mm | 620 mm |
| straight between corners | 190 mm | **40 mm** — corners nearly tangent |
| span / spare | 2690 / 110 mm | 2700 / **100 mm**, exactly on the reserve floor |
| driven route per lap | 8.23 m | **7.03 m (-14%)** |
| model scale | 1:11.80 | **1:11.80, unchanged** — each lane is still 12 ft |
| MUTCD deviations | **two** (ratio + dashed edges) | **one** (ratio only) |

Two lanes restore a real centreline, so DU's `dash:gap = 1:2` would sit where
MUTCD actually puts a dash and the "dashed edge lines" deviation from DV
disappears. The costs are 14% fewer metres of driving per lap — which is 14%
fewer frames per lap for M3 — and a straight run of 40 mm, leaving essentially
no room for any further width growth.

**Single lane remains the BUILT configuration. It is now a choice rather than a
forced outcome, and Evan should get to re-decide it on correct numbers.**
Not changed unilaterally: the scene, `cad/marking_specs.py`'s dash placement,
and DV's option-2 decision all still describe single-lane.

## Stop sign placed and relocation PROVEN (the other half of this entry)

`stop_sign` mixin, placed as a STANDALONE entity `nSsqp4h-KxRYD1sUwje8t` —
standalone is what makes it relocatable, rather than baked into the street's
generated content.

- initial: `position "15 0 2.43"`, `rotation "0 -90 0"` (0.6 m off the lane
  edge, facing back down the lane at traffic travelling +X — confirmed by a
  focus snapshot from x=11.89 showing the sign face)
- **relocation proven, not assumed**: one `entityUpdate` moved it to
  `"-10 0 2.43"`, 25 m along the street, `getEntity` read back the new
  position, and no street rebuild was needed.

That satisfies PRD task Y.3's "NEW HARD REQUIREMENT — the sign must be
RELOCATABLE / REMOVABLE" **in the model**. It says nothing about the physical
mount, which is still unbuilt.

⚠️ **The 3DStreet sign is scale-correct and the PHYSICAL sign is deliberately
NOT.** Evan decided 2026-08-10 (Appendix Y) on "auxiliary detection head + an
oversized (non-scale) printed sign", because pixel SHARE governs whether the
training objective cares and 0 of 899 cone pixels survived reconstruction in
`ml/compare_encoders.py`. So do not derive the printed sign's size from the
1:11.80 scale — a scale-correct 30 in sign would be 64.6 mm, and the standing
decision is deliberately larger than that. The scaled figure is a reference
point for how far off-scale the real one is, nothing more.

# Appendix DX - Track switched to TWO lanes at 250mm each (1.613x, deliberate); lane/road conflation refactored out; cornering clearance now 29.6mm, below the 50mm EST minimum (2026-09-06, ~16:22 CDT)
**Evan: "switch to 2"**, then — once the cost surfaced — the narrow-lane
variant. The track is now a two-lane road, one lane per direction.

## The decision, in two steps

Two lanes at the `SIM_TRANSFER_SPEC` 2.0x rule need a **620 mm** road, and at
that width the 3x3 grid fits **only at R=500** — the optimistic end of the
frozen 500-670 mm band. That would commit corner geometry before T2's turning
test has run, which the project's own hard rule forbids. Measured, not
reasoned:

| R | 1 lane (310 mm road) | 2 lanes @ 620 mm | widest 2-lane that fits |
|---|---|---|---|
| 500 | fits, 110 mm spare | fits, 100 mm spare | 350 mm/lane |
| 550 | fits | **REFUSES** (span 2820 > 2800) | 250 mm/lane |
| 600 | fits | **REFUSES** (span 3020) | 150 mm — narrower than the car |
| 670 | refuses | refuses | — |

**Evan's call: two lanes at 250 mm each (1.613x car width), road 500 mm.** That
buys back R=550 as well as R=500. 1.613x sits inside Duckietown's measured
1.4-1.6x band, so it is a sourced deviation from the 2.0x rule, not an
arbitrary one.

## Real output at the new geometry

    lane width      250 mm per direction (1.613 x car -- DELIBERATELY under the 2.0x rule)
    road width      500 mm total, 2 lanes -- THIS is what the grid geometry consumes
    street pitch    1100 mm  (straight between corners 100 mm)
    span            2700 mm of 2800 usable -> 100 mm SPARE
    driven route    figure-8 through the centre intersection, 7.51 m
    track_layout_v2 self_check: PASS

Lap length 8.23 -> **7.51 m** (-8.7%), not the -14% the 620 mm road would have
cost, because the narrower road leaves pitch at 1100 mm instead of 1040.

## ⚠️ A COST I UNDERSTATED WHEN EVAN CHOSE

When offering the 1.613x option I quoted **"47.5 mm clearance per side"**. That
is the STATIC figure, `(lane - car)/2`. **The cornering figure is 29.6 mm**,
because off-tracking at the measured 185.95 mm wheelbase eats 35.9 mm at
R=500:

| lane | off-track @ R=500 | clearance/side | vs MIN_SIDE_CLEARANCE 50 mm |
|---|---|---|---|
| 310 mm | 35.9 mm | **59.6 mm** | OK |
| **250 mm** | 35.9 mm | **29.6 mm** | **BELOW MINIMUM** |

`cad/vehicle_envelope.py`'s `MIN_SIDE_CLEARANCE = 0.050` is itself an EST and
nothing asserts against it, so no check failed — the report simply prints
`TOO LONG` on every wheelbase row now. **This is a real consequence of the
narrow lane and Evan should get to revisit it knowing the right number.** Not
changed unilaterally.

## ROOT-CAUSE REFACTOR: `lane` and `road` were one variable

This is the fix that matters beyond today. `cad/track_layout_v2.py` used a
single `lane` variable to mean BOTH the per-direction lane width AND the total
paved width the grid geometry consumes. That conflation is exactly what
produced the misreading in Appendix DV and the arithmetic error in DW.

Now separated, and the separation is load-bearing rather than cosmetic:

- `LANE = LANE_TO_CAR * CAR_WIDTH` — one lane, one direction (250 mm)
- `LANES = 2`
- `ROAD = LANES * LANE` — total paved width (500 mm), **what `span`,
  `best_straight`, `check_fits`, the SVG stroke widths and the intersection
  boxes all consume**

Function parameters renamed `lane` -> `road` throughout, and `build()` now
returns `road`, `lane` and `lanes` as three distinct keys. The JSON gains
`lanes_per_street`, `lane_width_m_PER_DIRECTION` and `road_width_m_TOTAL` in
place of the ambiguous `lane_width_m`.

**Self-check change worth flagging:** the loop that asserted R=500/550/600 all
build now asserts 500/550 build and **600/670 REFUSE**. R=600 fitted at one
lane and does not at two. That is the second lane's real price, and it is now
pinned by a check rather than left to be rediscovered.

## Scale moved, and landed almost back where it started

Narrowing the lane to 250 mm moves the DERIVED scale from **1:11.80 to
1:14.63** — almost exactly the 1:14 the PRD carried all along.
**That is a coincidence, not a vindication.** 1:14 was a round number chosen
against a 130 mm ESTIMATE; 1:14.63 is derived from a measured 155 mm car under
a different lane rule. They agree by accident and would diverge the moment
either input moves. Recorded in `cad/marking_specs.py`'s docstring so nobody
later reads it as "1:14 was right after all".

New marking table at 1:14.63: normal line **6.94-10.42 mm**, stop line
**20.83-41.67 mm**, dash **62.6 / 125.2 mm** at 40 cycles per lap.

## The dashed-edge deviation is DELETED

Appendix DV put the dash on the lane edges because a single-lane road has no
centreline — a second MUTCD deviation stacked on DU's ratio compression. Two
lanes restore a real centreline, so **the dash is now ordinary MUTCD placement
and only the RATIO deviation remains.** `marking_specs.py`'s docstring block
had accumulated three layers of correction and was rewritten to one current
statement; the DV/DW/DX trail lives in the record, not in a docstring.

## `cad/vehicle_envelope.py` kept in step

- `max_car_width`'s divisor was a hardcoded `2.0` encoding "road = 2 x car"
  (one lane at the 2.0x rule). Now `ROAD_TO_CAR = LANES * LANE_TO_CAR` =
  **3.226**.
- Its cross-file drift guard now also pins `LANES` and `LANE_TO_CAR`, so the
  two files cannot disagree about the lane rule.
- Its clearance report had a hardcoded **0.130** car width and a caption
  reading "lane 260 mm". The caption went stale the instant the lane rule
  changed, which is what exposed it. Both now use the MEASURED 155 mm car.
  (Scope note: switching the table off the 130 mm estimate is slightly beyond
  "switch to two lanes" — done because my change is what made the caption
  wrong, and a report about whether the car fits should not use a superseded
  estimate.)

## 3DStreet scene rebuilt

Old single-lane street removed; new `managed-street-c4dxk0ug5`, 40 m, two
12 ft lanes, **dashed yellow centreline** (`short-dashed-stripe-yellow`) and
**solid white edges** (`solid-stripe`). Verified by close-up snapshot, not by
read-back alone — the lesson from Appendix DV, where a read-back echoed an
invalid striping id that rendered solid.

Note the 3DStreet scene is **unchanged by the 250-vs-310 mm choice**: it is
full-scale, so each lane is a 12 ft lane either way. The model scale is ours,
not its.

## Process slip

**I pre-cited "Appendix DX" in code comments before the script assigned the
letter** — the same rule I caught myself breaking in Appendix DU and then broke
again here, this time writing it to disk in three files rather than catching it
first. The letter happened to match again. The check after this entry is
whether the references are right, not whether I guessed well.

# Appendix DY - Marking + substrate layout built; the seam rule was enforced by nothing; MARK_W was 2.4-3.6x too wide (1506g -> 627g); the dash target assumed a centreline through intersections (2026-09-06, ~16:38 CDT)
Evan: "plan out a street layout". The plan-view geometry was already committed
(Appendix DX); what did not exist was the layer on top of it — where markings
stop, and how the board is physically cut. New file `cad/marking_layout.py`,
plus two defect fixes in `cad/track_layout_v2.py`.

## Two defects fixed first, one of them mine and committed

**1. `track_layout_v2.py:542` reported the road width as the lane width.**
`"lane_width_m_PER_DIRECTION": g["road"]` — both that field and
`road_width_m_TOTAL` emitted 0.4999…, when the lane is 0.25. Cause: in the DX
change I ran a blanket `g["lane"]` -> `g["road"]` replace across the SVG
writer, and it also caught the JSON field I had inserted one step earlier in the
same script. `build()` itself was always correct.
**Shipped in `415178d`.** This is the lane/road conflation that DX exists to
end, reintroduced by the very edit that fixed it — the blanket replace was the
mechanism.

**2. `MARK_W = 0.025` contradicted the derived line width — every filament
figure was inflated 2.4-3.6x.** `marking_specs.py` derives the MUTCD normal
line at **6.94-10.42 mm** at 1:14.63; `MARK_W` was a 25 mm `EST` predating that
file. Deleted, and `print_plan` now sources the width from `marking_specs`
(6 in / 10.42 mm, the wide end — easier to lay and more visible at 64x64).

    filament_g  1506 g -> 627 g          (real output, not projected)
    all-lines   3514 g -> 1464 g

These numbers have been quoted in the hybrid-vs-225-panels argument since
Appendix AX. The argument's CONCLUSION is unaffected — 627 g against ~12,600 g
for solid panels is if anything a stronger case — but the figures in the older
entries were computed on the 25 mm estimate and should be read as such.

## `cad/marking_layout.py` — the layout itself

Owns **no dimensions**: geometry from `track_layout_v2.build()`, dimensions from
`marking_specs.table()`, and a drift guard proving it still agrees with both.
Both loaded lazily inside functions, because `marking_specs.self_check` already
loads `track_layout_v2` and a module-level import would be a cycle.

**THE TWO TILINGS — a distinction no document had ever drawn.** Substrate panels
(foam board / coroplast) and printed marking strips are different objects.
`gotchas.md`'s rule — *a seam running perpendicular to travel reads as a STOP
BAR to the model* — constrains the SUBSTRATE. The only tiling ever computed
before now (`print_plan`'s `ceil(printed_len / 0.200)` = 122) counts STRIPS.
**So the one physical constraint on tiling was enforced by nothing.**

Now satisfied by construction: substrate panels are strips running ALONG each
street's travel axis, so every seam is parallel to travel. At a 500 mm road and
`PANEL_MAX_W = 250 mm` that is exactly two strips per street — and **the single
longitudinal seam lands on the centreline, where the centreline marking covers
it.** Straight streets end up with no visible seam at all. Intersections are
single uncut 500 mm squares; a seam inside a box would cross travel on one of
the two streets whichever way it were oriented.

Real output:

    CENTRELINE   12 segments, 7200 mm total, dash 62.6 / gap 125.2, 36 dashes laid
    STOP LINES   28, width 20.83-41.67 mm
    NOT MARKED   [(-1.1, -1.1), (1.1, 1.1)]  never driven
    SUBSTRATE    24 street strips (2 per road at 250 mm) + 9 uncut 500 mm squares

## Three design calls, each a judgement call and recorded as one

**Centreline breaks at every intersection** — MUTCD drops it through a junction.
Free realism, and a line running straight through a junction is exactly the cue
a model would use to decide it may proceed.

**Stop lines on every approach of every driven intersection, or none.** This
falls out of Appendix Y.3's own logic. Y.3 requires the SIGN be relocatable so
the policy cannot memorise its position. **A painted stop line is exactly as
much of a positional giveaway as a fixed sign** — painting a subset would
reintroduce the leak Y.3 closes. All four approaches of all seven driven
intersections: 28 lines, and the line then carries no information about where
the sign is on a given run.

**The two undriven intersections are not painted.** The route uses 7 of 9;
(-1.1,-1.1) and (+1.1,+1.1) are the ends of the diagonal the figure-8 never
touches. ⚠️ **Honest cost:** the streets still physically cross there, so an
unmarked crossing can appear in peripheral frames. Small at 64x64, but it is a
real domain gap, recorded rather than assumed away.

## ⚠️ THE DASH TARGET WAS COMPUTED ON AN ASSUMPTION THAT IS FALSE

`marking_specs.TARGET_DASH_CYCLES = 40` sized the dash so one lap shows 40
cycles. It divided the FULL 7.51 m route by the cycle length — which assumes the
centreline runs through intersections. It does not, by the decision above.

    route            7507 mm
    inside boxes     4000 mm (53%)  -- 8 box traversals, no centreline in any
    carries a dash   3507 mm
    cycles per lap   18.7           vs TARGET_DASH_CYCLES = 40

**Over half the driven route is inside an intersection box**, so the lap
delivers **18.7 cycles, not 40** — under half the design target, and the target
was the entire reason for deviating from MUTCD's ratio in the first place
(Appendix DU: MUTCD's 1:3 was rejected for giving too few dashes at this scale).

Two ways out, neither taken here: accept 18.7, or shrink the cycle to ~87.5 mm
(dash 29.2 / gap 58.3) so 40 cycles land on the 3507 mm that actually carries
one. **Evan's call. Not decided.** Note the second option pushes the dash toward
the printer's practical floor — `MIN_PRINTED_FEATURE_MM = 0.8` is far below it,
so printability is not the constraint, but a 29 mm dash at 64x64 is.

## Verification — every new check shown to FAIL, not merely to pass

    track_layout_v2 self_check: PASS
    vehicle_envelope self_check: PASS
    marking_specs   self_check: PASS
    marking_layout  self_check: PASS

Each new check re-run against a deliberately broken input:

    1 seam-rule        : FIRES -> street-NS: seam EW is not parallel to travel NS
    2 strips-per-road  : FIRES -> strips_per_road = 3
    3 centreline-in-box: FIRES -> centreline run (-0.850,-0.250) overlaps box (-1.750,-0.450)
    4 stop-line-driven : FIRES -> 29

Also fixed, because my own changes made them wrong: `track_layout_v2.py`'s
header docstring still carried the single-lane R-band table (lane 310 mm), and
the `LANE_TO_CAR` comment quoted only the 47.5 mm STATIC clearance without the
29.6 mm cornering figure from Appendix DX.

One check caught a fragility of mine during development: comparing the undriven
intersection coords to `g["pitch"]` by equality failed, because the coords are
rounded to 6 dp while pitch is `1.0999999999999999`. Now compared with
tolerance.

# Appendix DZ - 3x3 grid recreated in 3DStreet at 1:14.63 -- street NETWORK only: no curved corners, no figure-8, and it contradicts DY's marking layout at every intersection (2026-09-06, ~17:26 CDT)
Evan: "recreate the layout in 3dstreet". Done as far as 3DStreet can go, which
is less than the whole layout — and the gap is the point of this entry.

## What was built

Six managed streets on a 3x3 grid, scale-converted from `track_layout_v2.py`
at 1:14.63:

| model | full scale in the scene |
|---|---|
| street pitch 1100 mm | **16.0934 m** |
| span 2700 mm | street length **39.5 m** |
| road 500 mm (2 x 250) | **7.3152 m** (2 x 12 ft) |

Three streets running along Z at x = -16.0934, 0, +16.0934; three running along
X at z = -16.0934, ~0, +16.0934. Every street: two drive lanes, dashed yellow
centreline (`short-dashed-stripe-yellow`), solid white edges (`solid-stripe`),
no vehicle models.

Verified by read-back, not by the picture: `managed-street-2lwz3p134` reports
`position "0 0 16.0934"`, `rotation "0 90 0"`, `length: 39.5`.

Scene retitled and saved:
<https://3dstreet.app/#/scenes/ac08e443-9733-47aa-bb53-62a032a0d712>

## WHAT IS MISSING, AND IT IS THE IMPORTANT HALF

**No corner arcs and no figure-8 route.** 3DStreet has no curved streets
(Appendix AM), so the R=500 mm rounded corners — the geometry that makes this a
drivable track rather than a street plan — cannot be drawn. The junctions here
are square.

**So this render shows the street NETWORK, not the driven track.** It is
correct about pitch, span, cross-section, lane count and marking style, and
silent about the thing the car actually follows. HANDOFF already said 3DStreet
could not do plan-view geometry; this is that claim demonstrated rather than
asserted, and the render should be captioned as a network diagram wherever it
is used.

**It also does NOT implement Appendix DY's marking layout.** DY decided the
centreline BREAKS at every intersection (MUTCD drops it through a junction). In
the scene the yellow dashes run straight through all nine crossings, because
managed streets are independent entities and 3DStreet has no intersection-aware
marking logic. Stop lines are absent for the same reason. **The authority on
markings remains `cad/marking_layout.py`; this scene contradicts it at every
intersection and must not be used to check marking placement.**

## Technique, worth not rediscovering

- **`managedStreetCreate` has no rotation parameter.** Applying
  `entityUpdate(component="rotation", value="0 90 0")` afterwards works, and
  rotates about the street's own centre so its `position` is unaffected
  (`street-align: length: middle`).
- **An unrotated managed street runs its LENGTH along Z**, width along X. Read
  off the segment children, which sit at `position "-1.8288 0.15 0"` and
  `"1.8288 0.15 0"` — offsets on X. The plan view had suggested the opposite;
  the child positions are the reliable signal.
- ⚠️ **After a plan snapshot the camera gets stuck top-down.** `focus`,
  `birdseye` and `closeup` then all return a byte-identical frame (85200 bytes,
  camera `y=94.89, tiltDeg 90`). `closeup` had moved the camera earlier the
  same session, when the scene held one street. **No angled portfolio render
  was produced.** Unresolved; try the view types BEFORE a plan snapshot next
  time, or move the camera another way.
- The `zoomOut: 1.3` argument to `takeSnapshot` timed out ("Timed out waiting
  for the plan view to zoom out"); plain `plan` succeeded.

## Two shortcuts taken, both marked

- **The centre E-W street sits at `z = 0.0001`, not 0** — a 0.1 mm offset to
  avoid being exactly coplanar with the centre N-S street at the origin. A hack
  against z-fighting, not a geometric choice; it is 0.0001 m at full scale,
  i.e. 7 nanometres at model scale, so it changes nothing physical.
- **All nine intersections have two road surfaces overlapping at the same
  elevation (0.15).** Z-fighting was not visible in the render, but it is
  present in the scene structure and may show at other camera angles.

## Unchanged

Nothing on disk changed this session — no CAD file, no generator output. This
was scene work only. `cad/track_layout_v2.py` remains the authority on
geometry and `cad/marking_layout.py` on markings; the scene is downstream of
both and, as noted above, currently disagrees with the second.

# Appendix EA - LaneMaker speaks OpenDRIVE, which HAS the arc primitive 3DStreet lacks; figure-8 exported as .xodr; the route has 6 corners not 8 (2026-09-06, ~22:13 CDT)
Evan installed LaneMaker and asked whether I could reach it. Partly — and the
part that matters turned out to be a route around the limitation Appendix DZ
had just documented.

## What LaneMaker actually is, and what is reachable

`C:\Users\evan.EVANFREDY\Downloads\LaneMaker_0.9_Win64\Release\LaneMaker.exe`
— a Qt5 desktop GUI (Qt5Core/Gui/Widgets DLLs alongside it).

- **The executable: NOT reachable.** I can launch a process but have no screen
  or desktop control, so I cannot see or drive its window. The Browser pane is
  a browser, not a desktop.
- **Its files: fully reachable.** And that is the whole story, because
  `SampleMaps/` holds `bridge.xodr` and `traffic_test.xodr` — **OpenDRIVE**,
  the ASAM road-network standard that CARLA, esmini and SUMO all read. Plain
  XML.

⚠️ Two things about LaneMaker I did NOT establish: whether it can IMPORT
`.xodr` (it may be export-only, in which case the file below is for a different
consumer), and whether the GUI needs a base map to start from. `gmp-10.dll` and
`mpfr-6.dll` in the Release folder are the CGAL exact-arithmetic stack, which
suggests exact geometric predicates — inferred from the DLL names, not verified.

## WHY THIS MATTERS: OpenDRIVE HAS THE PRIMITIVE 3DSTREET LACKS

Appendix DZ recorded that 3DStreet cannot represent the R=500 mm corner arcs,
because a managed street there is a cross-section extruded along a STRAIGHT
line. OpenDRIVE's `<planView>` takes `<line>`, `<arc>`, `<spiral>` and
`<paramPoly3>`. Counted in LaneMaker's own samples:

    line         bridge=280    traffic=64
    arc          bridge=356    traffic=101
    spiral       bridge=286    traffic=128
    paramPoly3   bridge=98     traffic=22

So the geometry that makes this a track rather than a street plan is a native
primitive in a format now sitting on Evan's disk. `<spiral>` is a clothoid —
a real transition curve between straight and arc, which `track_layout_v2.py`
does not model at all.

## New file: `cad/export_xodr.py`

Emits the driven route as one closed OpenDRIVE road: **14 geometries, 8 line
and 6 arc**, at full scale by default (x14.6304, so lane widths are a real
3.6576 m rather than an absurd 0.25 m). `--model-scale` writes the physical
2.7 m track instead. Both written: `cad/track_figure8.xodr` and
`cad/track_figure8_model.xodr`.

    scale           FULL, x14.6304 (the 1:14.63 model rendered at real-world size)
    geometries      14  (8 line, 6 arc)
    corner radius   7.3152 m  -> curvature 0.136702
    lane width      3.6576 m each, 2 lanes
    route length    109.9093 m
    turns           3 left + 3 right, net turn 0 (balanced figure-8)

## THE ROUTE HAS 6 CORNERS, NOT 8 — derived here for the first time

`track_layout_v2.py`'s docstring has always claimed "3 lefts + 3 rights" and
its self-check 4 tests that the turning is balanced, but nothing had ever
derived WHERE those six corners are, and the route has eight vertices.

The two extras are both `(0, 0)`. The route visits the centre intersection
twice, and **on both passes the heading does not change** — it runs straight
through. So those vertex pairs merge into straights of 2.2 m rather than
producing arcs. Six corners remain.

Arithmetic, every term checkable:

    2 merged straights   2 * (2.2 - 2R) = 2 * 1.2  = 2.4 m
    4 single straights   4 * (1.1 - 2R) = 4 * 0.1  = 0.4 m
    6 arcs               6 * R*pi/2     = 6*0.7854 = 4.7124 m
    total                                           7.5124 m

The 4 x 0.1 m term is the 100 mm straight-between-corners that Appendix DX
reported, arrived at independently.

## A mistake worth recording, because it produced a real number

The length check failed first time at `(7.512388980384689, 7.507028447306314)`
— a 5.36 mm gap I had budgeted 0.5 mm for. Discretization can only account for
about 0.1 mm (240 chords across 6 arcs, each fractionally shorter than its
arc), so the gap was not what I assumed.

Cause: I re-derived the polyline length with an open sum `i..i+1`, while
`track_layout_v2.path_len` closes the loop (`np.diff(..., append=p[:1])`) and
so counts a **5.042 mm closing chord** the open sum misses.
7.507028 + 0.005042 = 7.512070 exactly.

Fixed by comparing against `path_len` itself rather than a reimplementation of
it — the same "the generator is the authority" rule from Appendix DS that I
broke in DW. **The exact decomposition (7.512389 m) is the MORE accurate
figure**; `path_len`'s 7.512070 carries 0.32 mm of polyline artifact.

## Self-checks, and one defect of mine they did not catch

    export_xodr self_check: PASS

Five checks: 6 arcs with 3 left and 3 right; total length against
`path_len` within 1 mm; **continuity — every geometry starts exactly where the
previous ends in BOTH position and heading** (a gap there is a road that
teleports); net turning exactly zero (an oval would total 2*pi); and the XML
reparses with an `<arc>` and a centre-lane `<roadMark>` present.

**Not caught by any check: I left an `if False else` dead branch in
`build_xml`** computing lane width two ways, one of them nonsense. Found by
re-reading the diff, not by a test. Removed; both widths are now plainly
`model dimension x scale`. Also fixed a print line that rendered the scale as
a meaningless `1:1.00`, and a docstring claiming a 0.03 mm discretization gap
when the real figure is 0.32 mm.

## What the file deliberately does NOT contain

The 3x3 grid, the 9 intersections, junction records, and lane links between
roads. A figure-8 self-intersects and OpenDRIVE models that with a junction
plus connecting roads; this emits the route as a single road that simply
crosses itself geometrically. Valid OpenDRIVE, and the smallest thing that
answers "does LaneMaker load our geometry at all".

⚠️ **Two reasons it may still be rejected, both untested:** the road links to
itself (`predecessor` and `successor` both `elementId="0"`), which is correct
for a closed loop but unusual; and no junction is declared at the crossing, so
a tool validating topology may object. **Whether it loads is Evan's test — I
cannot drive the GUI.** Either outcome is informative and neither has been
observed yet.

# Appendix EB - LaneMaker DOES import xodr and named its own blocker: a roadRunnerProfile vendor block, schema decoded from the binary and samples (2026-09-06, ~22:17 CDT)
Follow-up to Appendix EA, written four minutes later. EA closed with "whether
it loads is Evan's test". He tested it. **LaneMaker DOES import `.xodr`** — it
parsed the file and rejected it for one specific reason:

    xodr map needs to contain custom LaneProfile!

That is a far better outcome than a generic failure: import works, and the
error is actionable.

## The requirement is a RoadRunner vendor extension, not standard OpenDRIVE

My first grep for `LaneProfile` in the SampleMaps returned **zero hits in both
files**, which looked like a dead end. It was a bad grep — the element is not
named "LaneProfile".

Found by reading strings out of `LaneMaker.exe` (read-only inspection, ~4 MB
binary):

    'xodr map needs to contain custom LaneProfile!'
    'LaneProfile::Convertside'
    'LaneProfile::Apply'
    'LaneProfile::Apply empty'
    'roadRunnerProfile'          <- the actual element name
    'roadRunnerBoundaryHide'
    './/elevationProfile//elevation'   <- it parses by XPath
    './/lanes//laneOffset'
    './/lane'

`roadRunnerProfile` IS in the samples — 544 occurrences in `traffic_test.xodr`
alone. It is a RoadRunner (MathWorks) extension, and it sits as the LAST child
of `<road>`, after `<objects>`.

The binary also confirms the CGAL guess from EA, which was inference there and
is evidence here: `D:/Dev/vcpkg/installed/x64-windows/include\CGAL/
Intersections_2/Line_2_Segment_2.h`. Other strings show the internal model is
roads + junctions with overlap resolution ("Overlap zone between roads {} & {}
can't be determined. Neither boundary pair intersects.").

## Schema, decoded from the samples

```xml
<roadRunnerProfile>
  <left>
    <section type_s="12714" laneCount="2" offsetX2="1" />
    <section type_s="4294967295" laneCount="2" offsetX2="1" />
  </left>
  <right>
    <section type_s="0" laneCount="2" offsetX2="-1" />
  </right>
</roadRunnerProfile>
```

| attribute | meaning | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `type_s` | section start, **s in CENTIMETRES** | road 0 length 127.14 m → 12714; road 1 226.72 m → 22671 |
| `4294967295` | UINT32_MAX, terminator on the `<left>` list | appears only as a second left entry |
| `laneCount` | **DRIVING** lanes on that side, medians NOT counted | road 0 left has ids 1,2,3 but lane 1 is `type="median"` → laneCount 2 |
| `offsetX2` | `laneOffset / laneWidth * 2`, i.e. offset in half-lane units | **verified across all 272 roads**: −1.625/3.25×2 = −1, +1.625 → +1, +3.25 → +2, 0 → 0 |

`offsetX2` is the one I am confident in — it holds on every road in the file
without exception.

## What is emitted, and what is still a guess

`cad/export_xodr.py` now writes, for our 1-lane-each-way road with
`laneOffset = 0`:

    <roadRunnerProfile>
      <left>
        <section type_s="10991" laneCount="1" offsetX2="0" />
        <section type_s="4294967295" laneCount="1" offsetX2="0" />
      </left>
      <right>
        <section type_s="0" laneCount="1" offsetX2="0" />
      </right>
    </roadRunnerProfile>

10991 = the 109.9093 m route in centimetres. A self-check now asserts the
`<left>` `type_s` equals the road length in centimetres, so that unit cannot
silently drift.

⚠️ **NOT understood, and it may still be refused:** why `<left>` carries a
length-in-cm section PLUS a UINT32_MAX terminator while `<right>` carries a
single `type_s="0"`. The asymmetry is consistent across the samples but I have
no reading of it I would defend. **And no sample road has a 1+1 layout without
a median** — every two-way road there has one — so this mirrors road 0's SHAPE
with our lane counts rather than copying a true analogue.

**If it is still refused, the cheap end to the guessing is ground truth: draw
any road in LaneMaker, save it, and read the profile it writes.** One minute of
Evan's time beats any further inference from samples that do not contain our
case.

## Process note

While decoding `offsetX2` I dumped a per-road table for all 272 roads into the
transcript — hundreds of lines where a dozen would have proved the same
relationship. Uncapped output on an exploratory query. The finding stands; the
method wasted context.

# Appendix EC - Bisection ladder: all 4 probes load, so self-link AND self-intersection are both harmless; the crashing file is byte-identical to a working one (2026-09-06, ~23:11 CDT)
Follow-up to Appendix EB. Evan reported LaneMaker **crashing** on the
profile-bearing `.xodr` rather than rejecting it. A bisection ladder settled it,
and both of my hypotheses were wrong.

## The crash was diagnosed from Windows crash dumps, not guessed

Two minidumps in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CrashDumps\` (`LaneMaker.exe.2188.dmp` 22:22,
`LaneMaker.exe.41188.dmp` 22:33). Parsed the MINIDUMP_EXCEPTION_STREAM
directly — no debugger needed, the format is documented:

    thread 42208  code 0xC0000409  fault address 0x00007FF888D4527E  params=1
    exception info ['0x7']

`0xC0000409` with parameter `7` is **FAST_FAIL_FATAL_APP_EXIT** — the MSVC
runtime's `std::terminate`/`abort` path. **An unhandled C++ exception, not
memory corruption.** Identical fault address in both dumps, so deterministic
and the same code path. That reading fits the binary's CGAL paths and its
`Rethrowing unknown exception in logger` string.

## The bisection ladder — `export_xodr.py --probe`

Four files, each adding one of the three ways our road differs from every road
in LaneMaker's own samples:

| probe | adds | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 straight | one straight road, 1 lane each way, no links | **loads** |
| 2 arc | + one arc (the curve path) | **loads** |
| 3 open8 | + the full figure-8 geometry, still no self-link | **loads** |
| 4 closed8 | + the self-link | **loads** |

**All four load.** Both of my prime suspects are dead:

- **The self-link is harmless.** No sample road links to itself
  (`predecessor`/`successor` with `elementType="road"` and its own id) — all 272
  link to junctions — so I expected it to be rejected. It is not.
- **The self-intersection is harmless.** Probe 3 crosses itself with no junction
  declared. LaneMaker loads it. My CGAL-overlap hypothesis, based on the binary's
  `Overlap zone between roads {} & {} can't be determined` string, was wrong.

Evan also observed that **probes 3 and 4 render identically**, which is correct
and worth stating: the self-link is topology metadata, not geometry, so it
changes nothing renderable.

## THE FILE CONTENT WAS NEVER THE CAUSE

`probe_4_closed8.xodr` and `cad/track_figure8.xodr` differ **only in two `name`
attributes**. Everything else — all 14 geometries, the lane section, the
roadRunnerProfile — hashes identically (`47c933c463da9685` over all non-`name`
lines).

Probe 4 loads. The byte-equivalent `track_figure8.xodr` crashed. So the crash
did not come from the file's content.

**Most likely: Evan opened the PRE-PROFILE attachment.** I sent one `.xodr`
before adding `roadRunnerProfile` and another after; both sat in the chat. The
earlier one produces the LaneProfile error, and dismissing that dialog is a
plausible path into the abort. Both dumps postdate the fixed file being sent,
but the older attachment was still there to click.

⚠️ **NOT CONFIRMED.** The one variable left is the `name` string itself —
`"figure-8 route"` and `"Autonomous Car Project figure-8"` contain spaces and a
hyphen where the probes say `"probe"`. It would be absurd for that to abort a
parser, and I do not believe it, but I have been wrong twice in this thread and
the test is free: open `cad/track_figure8.xodr` from the repo rather than from
a chat attachment. **Open at time of writing.**

## What this leaves standing

The exporter is validated as far as LaneMaker is concerned: **straights, arcs,
self-intersection and self-linking all import cleanly.** The figure-8 geometry
that 3DStreet structurally cannot represent (Appendix DZ) round-trips into a
real road-network tool.

Still not exported, unchanged from EA: the 3x3 grid, the 9 intersections,
junction records, lane links between roads.

## Process

Three separate times this session a backslash escape (`\\n`, `\\`) passed
through a quoted bash heredoc into Python and emitted a literal newline instead
of the escape, twice producing `SyntaxError: unterminated string literal`.
Fixed the last one by hoisting the XML declaration into a module constant
built with `chr(10)` so no escape crosses the boundary. **Stop writing
backslash escapes inside heredoc'd Python; use the Edit tool or `chr()`.**

# Appendix ED - 3x3 grid exported as OpenDRIVE (6 roads, no junctions); _add_road extracted from two near-duplicates, proven byte-identical (2026-09-07, ~00:08 CDT)
Evan: "make a track layout for the 3x3". Read as the standing gap Appendices EA
and EC both closed with — "still not exported: the 3x3 grid, the 9
intersections, junction records" — so: do for the grid what the figure-8 export
did.

## `export_xodr.py --grid`

Six roads, scale-converted from `track_layout_v2.py`, written to
`cad/track_grid3x3.xodr` (and `_model.xodr` with `--model-scale`):

    roads           6  (3 along Z, 3 along X)
    street length   39.5021 m each
    street pitch    16.0934 m
    road width      7.3152 m, 2 lanes
    crossings       9 (geometric only)

The same pitch and length as the 3DStreet scene built in Appendix DZ, so the
two independent representations of the grid agree.

## NO JUNCTION RECORDS, and that is a deliberate stop

The 9 crossings are geometric only — the roads simply overlap. **Appendix EC is
what licenses this**: probe 3 was a self-intersecting road with no junction
declared and LaneMaker loaded it, so crossing roads need none either.

Real junction topology — `<junction>` elements with connecting roads and lane
links between every approach — is a much larger job and only worth doing if the
tool needs to understand TURNS rather than just draw streets. Not attempted.

## A REFACTOR, because a third copy would have been the wrong move

`build_xml` and `_probe_xml` were near-duplicates I created earlier the same
session (EA, then EC's probe ladder). The grid would have made **three** places
holding the lane block, the `roadRunnerProfile` and the geometry loop.

Extracted `_add_road(root, rid, name, geoms, scale, self_link=False)`; all
three callers now use it, and `_probe_xml` is gone.

**The regression check that makes this trustworthy:** after the refactor,
regenerating `track_figure8.xodr`, `track_figure8_model.xodr` and all four
probe files left them **byte-identical** — none appears in `git status`. A
faithful extraction, proven rather than asserted.

New self-check group 7 pins the grid: 6 roads, unique ids, exactly one straight
geometry each, a `roadRunnerProfile` on each, all lengths equal, the street
coordinates landing on 3 values per axis, and `span == 2 * pitch + road`.

## What neither file shows

`track_grid3x3.xodr` is the street NETWORK — 6 crossing straights, which is
what `track_layout_v2.py` describes. `track_figure8.xodr` is the driven PATH,
with the R=500 mm rounded corners. **Neither file contains both.** The corners
exist only in the figure-8 export; the grid export has square crossings. Worth
saying plainly because the 3DStreet scene has the same split and it would be
easy to mistake either for "the track".

## Process, third time

Hit the bash-heredoc backslash bug AGAIN — `\\n` inside
`print(f"\\n-> {out}")` emitted a literal newline and produced
`SyntaxError: unterminated f-string literal`. This was one turn after writing
the rule against it into Appendix EC. Fixed with the Edit tool.

**The rule is not working as written.** Restating it as a mechanical one:
inside a heredoc'd Python script, do not type a backslash at all. If a newline
is needed in output, call `print()` with no argument, or build the string with
`chr(10)`. If an escape is genuinely required, use the Edit tool instead of the
heredoc.

# Appendix EE - Proper junctions: the kerb return radius reconciles the figure-8 with the grid; first cut crashed LaneMaker because 0 of 56 roads had a link (2026-09-07, ~00:25 CDT)
Evan: "do the curves too and proper intersections". Built, crashed LaneMaker,
diagnosed, fixed — all in one sitting. The crash was my defect and the
diagnosis is the useful part.

## THE KERB RETURN RADIUS IS THE DESIGN LEVER, and it reconciles two models

A turn confined to the bare intersection box (half-width `road/2` = 250 mm) has
radius `road/2 - lane/2` = **125 mm**, needing **56.1 degrees of steering lock**
at the measured 185.95 mm wheelbase. The servo-achievable estimate is 38.7
degrees (R_min 232.4 mm, Appendix DN). **The car could not make a right turn.**

Give the junction a kerb return radius Rt and the arcs become `Rt -/+ lane/2`:

| Rt | right | left | street segment | drivable vs R_min 232.4 mm |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 250 mm | 125 | 375 | 600 mm | left only |
| 375 mm | 250 | 500 | 350 mm | both |
| **500 mm** | **375** | **625** | **100 mm** | **both** |
| 625 mm | 500 | 750 | -150 mm | junctions would overlap |

At Rt = 500 mm the street segments come out at **100 mm — exactly the "straight
between corners" `track_layout_v2` already reports.** That is not a
coincidence: **the figure-8's R=500 sweeping corners ARE the junction turns.**
The route model and the junction model were always describing the same
geometry from two directions. A self-check now asserts every turn radius is at
least the servo estimate, so a radius change that makes the grid undrivable
fails loudly.

## A hypothesis I had, and the measurement that killed it

I suspected the R=500 route left the roadway on its corners, since an arc
tangent 500 mm from the vertex starts well outside a 250 mm box. Measured over
all 780 route points: **max offset 139.4 mm against a 250 mm half-width, 0
points off the roadway, 110.6 mm to spare.** My hand-check only considered the
approaching street; near a corner the path is covered by the CROSSING street's
pavement, and the min-distance-to-any-centreline metric sees that.

## `export_xodr.py --junctions`

    street segments 12  (1.463 m each at full scale)
    junctions       9   arms: 1x4-way, 4x3-way, 4x2-way
    connecting rds  44  (every legal movement, no U-turns)
    geometry        24 line, 32 arc

Arm counts fall out of the grid: corner junctions have 2 arms, edge junctions
3, the centre 4, giving 2 + 6 + 12 connections respectively = 44.

⚠️ **The grid is 91% junction and 9% street** — 1000 mm of junction diameter in
every 1100 mm of pitch. That follows directly from Rt=500 against pitch 1100.
Honest, but it means these "streets" are 100 mm stubs between large turning
areas, not a street grid in the ordinary sense.

## THE CRASH: a junction graph with no edges

Evan opened it; LaneMaker died. **A different crash from the earlier two** —
the dump says `0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION at 0x7FF7E8D430FB`, and that address
is in the EXE's own range, where the two crashes of Appendix EB/EC were
`0xC0000409 FAST_FAIL` at `0x7FF888...`, a system DLL. Not a thrown exception
this time: a bad pointer dereference inside LaneMaker's own code.

Cause, confirmed against the samples: **0 of my 56 roads had a `<link>`
element.** Every road in `traffic_test.xodr` has one. I generated the
`<junction>` blocks and the connecting roads, and the junctions pointed at the
roads — but **no road pointed back**. LaneMaker walks road -> junction ->
connecting road and dereferenced links that were not there.

The correct structure, read off the sample:

- a CONNECTING road links to **roads**:
  `<predecessor elementType="road" elementId="2" contactPoint="start"/>`
- a STREET road links to **junctions**:
  `<predecessor elementType="junction" elementId="0" contactPoint=""/>`

Fixed: `_set_link()` inserts `<link>` as the first child of `<road>` (OpenDRIVE
child order). Now 88 road-links (44 connectors x 2) + 24 junction-links
(12 streets x 2) = every road wired.

## A second defect the same fix exposed

I had hardcoded `laneLink from="-1"`. The sample's first connection is
`laneLink from="2"`. **Which lane arrives depends on which END of the street
touches the junction:** lane -1 runs in +s, so a car reaching a road's END is
in -1, while one reaching its START came the other way and is in +1.
Hardcoding -1 mislabels half the approaches. After the fix the distribution is
**22 `from="-1"` and 22 `from="1"`** — exactly half, as the geometry demands.

## The check that was missing, and now exists

Every geometry check passed on a file with no graph edges at all. **Geometry
checks cannot see a missing link.** New self-check 8d verifies TOPOLOGY: every
road has a non-empty `<link>`; every link target exists; connecting roads link
to roads and streets link to junctions (not the reverse); every
`incomingRoad`/`connectingRoad` in a `<connection>` resolves; and both approach
directions actually occur in the laneLinks.

Proven to fire, by stripping the links back out:

    FIRES -> road 0 has no <link>

Regression: every previously committed `.xodr` is unchanged.

## Honest status

**Whether the fixed file loads is untested** — I cannot drive the GUI. The
crash is diagnosed and the structural defect is real and fixed, but "fixed"
here means "matches the sample's structure and passes a topology check", not
"observed to open".

# Appendix EF - Evan's own LaneMaker export is ground truth: connecting roads must be ONE-WAY; that fix makes the file load; junction boundary and U-turns still missing (2026-09-07, ~00:33 CDT)
Evan exported a 3x3 grid from LaneMaker itself
(`~/Downloads/1122.xodr`) — the ground-truth reference I had asked for two
appendices earlier. It found a real defect, the fix made the file LOAD, and it
left two differences still open.

## THE FILE NOW LOADS. The defect was two-way connecting roads.

Appendix EE's junction export crashed with `0xC0000005 ACCESS_VIOLATION` inside
LaneMaker's own code. Against the reference, the cause is plain: **my
connecting roads were TWO-WAY.** A turn movement runs one way. All 47 of
LaneMaker's connecting roads have exactly one shape:

- `<right>` with lane `-1` and `<center>` with lane `0` — **no `<left>`
  element at all**
- `laneOffset a = +lane/2` (its `+1.625`), so the reference line sits on the
  lane's left edge
- a **LANE-level `<link>`** inside the lane: `<predecessor id=..>`,
  `<successor id=..>` — mine had none
- `roadRunnerProfile` with only `<right>`, `offsetX2="1"`

Fixed via a new `_add_oneway_road()`. Verified attribute by attribute against
the reference:

| | reference | mine after the fix |
|---|---|---|
| connecting roads with a `<left>` group | 0 of 47 | **0 of 44** |
| with a lane-level `<link>` | 47 of 47 | **44 of 44** |
| profile containing `<left>` | 0 of 47 | **0 of 44** |
| `laneOffset a` | +1.625 | **+1.8288** (our lane/2) |

**Evan confirms the file opens and the connections appear.** Self-check 8e now
pins the one-way invariant.

## TWO CORRECTIONS TO EARLIER APPENDICES

**The median is NOT required (corrects EB's suspicion).** EB flagged that no
sample road has a 1+1 layout without a median and treated it as a likely
blocker. Probes 1-4 (Appendix EC) load fine with exactly that layout, so a
median lane is not needed. LaneMaker writes one; it does not demand one.

**`offsetX2 = 0` was correct all along.** Seeing the reference's `+1`/`-1` I
started to "fix" mine and stopped when the arithmetic said otherwise:
`offsetX2 = laneOffset / laneWidth * 2`, and my two-way roads have
`laneOffset = 0`, so 0 is self-consistent. The reference's roads are +/-1
because their reference lines sit half a lane off centre. Both are right for
their own geometry — the EB decode holds.

## WHAT IS STILL BROKEN, and the evidence

Two symptoms remain, both reported by Evan:

1. **Connections only render on hover.**
2. **Starting the simulation crashes.**

The new dump is `0xC0000409 FAST_FAIL param 7` at `0x7FF888D4527E` — back to
`std::terminate` on an unhandled C++ exception, the SAME address as the two
crashes of Appendix EB, and NOT the ACCESS_VIOLATION that the one-way fix
cleared. So loading is genuinely fixed and the simulator throws on something
else.

Both symptoms point at the same missing element: **`<junction><boundary>`**,
which mine lacks entirely (0 of 9; the reference has 5 of 5). Junction graphics
are presumably generated from it — no boundary, nothing drawn except on
selection highlight. And the binary carries
`Overlap zone between roads {} & {} can't be determined. Neither boundary pair
intersects.`, which reads like the simulator resolving road overlaps FROM
boundaries.

**The boundary format, decoded from the reference:** two segments per ARM,
alternating

- `type="lane"` — a stretch along a CONNECTING road's outer edge
  (`roadID`, `sStart`, `sEnd`, `side`)
- `type="joint"` — ZERO-LENGTH (`sStart == sEnd`) on an INCOMING street road,
  where the junction meets it

Counts confirm it: the 4-arm junction has 4 joints + 4 lanes = 8 segments; the
3-arm junctions 3+3 = 6; the 2-arm junction 2+2 = 4.

**A second difference found the same way: LaneMaker INCLUDES U-turns.** Its
4-arm junction has 16 connections = 4x4, and its 3-arm ones have 9 = 3x3. Mine
excludes arm-to-same-arm movements (44 total). Whether the simulator needs them
is unknown.

## THE NEXT STEP IS A TEST, NOT A GUESS

I have guessed wrong three times in this thread (self-link, self-intersection,
median). Before building a boundary tracer — real work, and `side` and segment
ordering are both things I would be inferring — **the decisive question is
whether simulation crashes on LaneMaker's OWN `1122.xodr`.**

- If it crashes there too, the simulator needs something neither file has, or
  is simply fragile, and my file is not the cause.
- If it runs there, the boundary and/or the U-turn connections are mine to
  build.

One click, and it decides whether an hour of work is warranted. **Open at time
of writing.**

# Appendix EG - Simulation works on LaneMaker's own file, so the fault is ours; U-turns added (68 connections); the junction boundary trim cannot be derived and is left unbuilt (2026-09-07, ~00:45 CDT)
**Evan ran the decisive test: simulation WORKS on LaneMaker's own `1122.xodr`.**
That rules out the tool and puts the remaining fault squarely on my export —
which is exactly why the test was worth doing before building anything.

## U-turns added: the cheap, exact half of the gap

LaneMaker emits `k` arms -> `k*k` movements, U-turns included: its 4-arm
junction has 16 connections, its 3-arm ones 9, its 2-arm one 4. Mine excluded
arm-to-same-arm and had 44.

Now **80 roads, 68 connections** — 4x4 + 4x(3x3) + 4x(2x2) = 68, matching the
convention exactly. My own self-check caught the stale constant on the first
run (`AssertionError: 68` against `== 44`), and a new assert pins the rule
itself: `sum(len(arms)**2) == 68`.

⚠️ **The 24 U-turns are NOT drivable by this car.** A U-turn swings between two
lane centres `lane` apart, so its radius is `lane/2` = 125 mm model / 1.829 m
full — under the 232.4 mm servo-achievable R_min. They are emitted for FORMAT
CONFORMANCE only, and drivability check 8b now skips them **by design, with the
reason in-code**, rather than silently passing. The continuity check does NOT
skip them: all 68 arcs, including the 180-degree ones, land on their outgoing
lane in position and heading.

## The remaining gap, and the number I cannot derive

`<junction><boundary>` — mine has 0 of 9, the reference 5 of 5.

Structure decoded and confident: **2 segments per ARM**, alternating a
`type="lane"` stretch along a connecting road's outer edge with a ZERO-LENGTH
`type="joint"` on the incoming street. Counts confirm across all five of its
junctions (4 arms -> 4+4=8 segments, 3 arms -> 6, 2 arms -> 4).

**What I cannot derive is the trim.** Junction 0's lane segments run
`s = 0.948 .. 21.814` on a 22.763 m connector — symmetrically trimmed by
**0.949 m at each end** — and nothing in the file explains where 0.949 comes
from. It is not the lane width (3.25), not half of it (1.625). `side` and the
segment ordering would also be inferred. Three of my inferences in this thread
have been wrong (self-link, self-intersection, median), so this is flagged as
guesswork rather than attempted.

Also worth recording from the reference: its geometry is **21 line, 21 spiral,
18 arc, 6 paramPoly3**. The spirals are clothoid transitions between straight
and arc — real road alignment, which `export_xodr.py` does not model at all.
That is why Evan's grid is "not perfectly straight".

## RECOMMENDATION, and the reason for it

**Stop here and bank the exporter as "loads and renders correctly in LaneMaker;
simulation unsupported."** That is a real, honest result.

This is not on the critical path. The physical track is defined by
`cad/track_layout_v2.py` and `cad/marking_layout.py`, both complete and
self-checked. LaneMaker is a visualisation and validation nicety that has now
consumed a large share of a session, while three actual decisions sit
untouched: the dash density (18.7 cycles/lap against the 40 that justified
deviating from MUTCD at all), the cornering clearance (29.6 mm/side against the
50 mm EST), and THE ORDER ($411.45, all six BOM checks closed since
2026-09-05).

The boundary remains buildable if Evan wants it later; the structure above is
the head start.

# Appendix EH - NEGATIVE: U-turns did not fix the simulation crash (identical fault address); four hypotheses, four wrong, and every correct finding came from evidence (2026-09-07, ~00:50 CDT)
**NEGATIVE RESULT: adding U-turns did NOT fix the simulation crash.** Appendix
EG shipped 80 roads and 68 connections matching LaneMaker's `k` arms -> `k*k`
convention exactly. Evan tested it; the crash is unchanged.

## The evidence that it is unchanged, not merely similar

    LaneMaker.exe.3860.dmp   09-07 00:31:40  0xC0000409 FAST_FAIL p=7 @0x7FF888D4527E
    LaneMaker.exe.48748.dmp  09-07 00:49:02  0xC0000409 FAST_FAIL p=7 @0x7FF888D4527E

Byte-identical exception code, parameter and fault address across the
pre-U-turn and post-U-turn runs. `FAST_FAIL` parameter 7 is
`FATAL_APP_EXIT` — the MSVC `std::terminate`/abort path, i.e. an unhandled C++
exception. Same throw, same code path. The U-turn change moved nothing.

## FOUR HYPOTHESES, FOUR WRONG

For the record, because the pattern matters more than any one of them:

| # | hypothesis | how it died |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | the road self-link (`predecessor`/`successor` -> own id) crashes it | probe 4 loads (EC) |
| 2 | the self-intersecting road with no junction crashes it | probe 3 loads (EC) |
| 3 | a median lane is required | probes 1-4 load without one (EF) |
| 4 | U-turn connections are required | this entry — crash unchanged |

One hypothesis was RIGHT and it came from the reference file, not from
reasoning: connecting roads must be one-way (EF), which fixed loading.

**The lesson is about method, not about OpenDRIVE.** Every correct finding in
this thread came from evidence — a crash dump, a structural diff against
`1122.xodr`, a measurement. Every wrong one came from me reasoning about what a
tool "probably" needs. Four for four.

## What remains, and why it is not being attempted

`<junction><boundary>` is now the ONLY structural difference left between our
file and `1122.xodr`: ours has 0 of 9, the reference 5 of 5. Everything else
matches attribute by attribute.

⚠️ **That does not make it the cause.** It is the last thing I can SEE
differing; the fault could equally be a value inside an element we both have,
or something the structural diff does not surface at all. Calling it "the
cause" would be the fifth hypothesis.

And the trim still cannot be derived — junction 0's lane segments run
s = 0.948..21.814 on a 22.763 m connector, symmetrically trimmed by 0.949 m,
with nothing in the file explaining 0.949. Building it means inferring the
trim, `side`, and the segment ordering, on a hypothesis that four precedents
say is likely wrong.

## STANDING RECOMMENDATION, unchanged and now better supported

**Bank the exporter as "loads and renders correctly in LaneMaker; simulation
unsupported."** That is a real, honest, useful result: the figure-8 geometry
that 3DStreet structurally could not represent (Appendix DZ) round-trips into a
real road-network tool and draws correctly.

This is not on the critical path. `cad/track_layout_v2.py` and
`cad/marking_layout.py` define the physical track and are complete and
self-checked. Three actual decisions remain untouched: dash density (18.7
cycles/lap against the 40 that justified the MUTCD deviation), cornering
clearance (29.6 mm/side against the 50 mm EST), and THE ORDER ($411.45, all six
BOM Verify items closed since 2026-09-05).

If the boundary is attempted later, the structure in Appendix EG is the head
start — and it should be attempted as ONE timeboxed experiment with the
expectation that it may not be the cause, not as a fix.

# Appendix EI - Scheduled daily-audit: the controller's history feature is built from actions that never happened, and two self-checks pass on a broken artifact (2026-09-07 07:23 CDT)
Scheduled `daily-audit` cold sweep, 6 parallel workers over a 244-file manifest
(43 py, 5 ino + 1 h, 37 md, 10 xodr, 3 stl, 1 git hook; 135 json/npy/png under
`ml/runs/` excluded as generated run data). Findings only — nothing was changed.
Classified ACTIVE by churn override: the last audit was Appendix DH (2026-09-04)
but 23 non-audit commits landed after it.

## The one that matters

**`ml/train_controller.py:206` → `:240-241` — the controller's history feature is
built from actions that never happened.** When `train_actions_expert.npy` exists,
`act` is replaced with the DART expert relabels, and that same array is then
passed to `rnn_states()`, which feeds it to the frozen MDN-RNN's LSTM
(`:109-113`). `train_mdnrnn.py` only ever trains on executed actions from
`load_proc`. So `h_t` is conditioned on a counterfactual action sequence that did
not produce the observed latents — precisely on the recovery/noise frames where
the two arrays differ. This is a live confound for the Appendix Z.3 null result
("adding 6.67% recovery data left val MSE essentially unchanged"), and
`ml/diag_copycat.py` imports the same `rnn_states`, so the diagnostic meant to
validate the controller shares the contamination.
Fix: keep two arrays — raw executed `act` for the LSTM input, expert relabels
only for the BC loss target.

## Two guards that pass on a broken artifact

- `cad/vehicle_envelope.py:150-151` — the cross-file drift guard checks six names
  against `track_layout_v2.py` and omits `CAR_WIDTH`, which is defined
  independently in both files (`vehicle_envelope.py:50`, `track_layout_v2.py:92`,
  both 0.155). The constant every clearance number derives from is the one the
  guard cannot see, and `self_check: PASS` still prints.
- `cad/marking_specs.py:274` prints "40 cycles per lap" by construction from
  `TARGET_DASH_CYCLES = 40`. `cad/marking_layout.py` computes the real figure and
  prints `cycles per lap 18.7`. Both scripts self-check PASS; nothing asserts on
  the 2.1x gap. HANDOFF action item 1 already knows the real number is 18.7.

## Docs asserting what disk denies

- `HANDOFF.md:308` states "CURRENT, real output 2026-09-06 at lane 310 mm: route
  8.23 m, pitch 1190 mm, span 2690 mm, spare 110 mm". Running
  `python cad/track_layout_v2.py` now gives lane 250 mm, route 7.51 m, pitch
  1100 mm, span 2700 mm, spare 100 mm. HANDOFF's own line 95 already uses 7.51 m.
- `.claude/codebase-memory/track.md:288-298` asserts scale 1:11.80 and lane
  310 mm. `python cad/marking_specs.py` prints `SCALE 1:14.63 DERIVED`, lane
  250 mm. Lines 15 and 73 of the same file re-assert 1:11.80 against its own
  line 58, which records the move to 1:14.63.
  NOTE, and this corrected a worker: `README.md:3`'s "1/14-scale" is stale by
  0.63, not by 2.8 — 1:11.80 was itself superseded. The proposed fix to rewrite
  README to 1:11.80 would have made it worse and was rejected.
- `cad/track_layout_v1.py:440` writes the JSON key `car_width_m_MEASURED` while
  `:58` declares `CAR_WIDTH = 0.130 # UNMEASURED`. The committed
  `cad/track_layout_v1.json` still carries the truthful `car_width_m_ESTIMATE`,
  so regenerating flips a correct label to a false one — a direct violation of
  this project's CLAUDE.md rule that physical-world claims stay honest.
- `firmware/README.md:75` — "No control firmware exists. The serial protocol is
  designed on paper only." `firmware/uno_control/uno_control.ino` is 657 lines
  and flashed; `SERIAL_PROTOCOL.md:3` says IMPLEMENTED.
- `firmware/SERIAL_PROTOCOL.md:1` titles itself "DRAFT v0.1" while `:11` says it
  was bumped to v0.2 and `:3` says IMPLEMENTED. `:5` claims SELFTEST 39/39 for
  the 2026-09-02 flash the record puts at 49/49; the current source has 58
  checks.
- `.claude/codebase-memory/INDEX.md:9-11` understates three bins by 100-200 lines
  each (hardware.md 313 claimed / 466 actual; steering.md 141 / 339; track.md
  334 / 363) — the file whose job is tracking cap overage.
- `docs/research/2026-08-12_onboard-compute-selection.md` and
  `2026-08-12_pi5-alternatives.md` both still end on "Raspberry Pi 5 2GB — Buy."
  The project bought the 4GB Vilros kit; `dependencies.md:88` explains why.
  Neither brief carries a superseded note.
- `.mcp.json` runs `npx -y 3dstreet-mcp` with no version pin, so every session

## Partial failsafe, deliberate and documented

`firmware/uno_control/uno_control.ino:632-643` — on watchdog trip
(`WATCHDOG_MS = 150`) throttle goes to 0 immediately and `PIN_STBY` goes LOW
after `BRAKE_MS = 500`, a hardware Hi-Z disable of the TB6612. Steering is NOT
centred; the servo holds its last angle indefinitely. `SERIAL_PROTOCOL.md` §3.2
documents this as intentional (avoids a jerk). Recorded as a known shape of the
failsafe, not as a defect.

## Load-bearing negatives

Episode-level train/val splitting confirmed by running `splits.py` self-check.
Seeding covers torch + numpy + cuda in all four trainers. `models.py`,
`episode_writer.py`, `provenance.py` self-checks all PASS. Figure-8 closes to
<6e-10 m; all 80 roads in both junction `.xodr` files have resolvable links;
`export_xodr.py` regenerates byte-identical across three runs; both STLs are
manifold with volumes matching analytic values to 1e-14. The serial protocol's
CRC-8/SMBus matches byte-for-byte across doc, firmware and `host_test.py`, and
the fixed-frame design means no sender-controlled length can overrun `rxBuf`.
`scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit` fails CLOSED when the delegated scanner is
missing, requiring `CAR_ALLOW_UNGATED_COMMIT=1` to bypass. `docs/BOM.md` rows
sum to exactly the claimed $411.45. Every Uno pin in BOM/WIRING matches the
`PIN_*` constants.

# Appendix EJ - Fixed the DART action contamination in the controller: rnn_states() was fed the expert relabel instead of the executed sequence; the fix strengthens Z.3's negative, closed-loop unchanged at 0/9 (2026-09-07 ~10:32 CDT)
**WHAT:** Fixed the action-contamination bug the 2026-09-07 07:23 CDT scheduled
audit found (Appendix EI, "the one that matters"): `ml/train_controller.py`
overwrote `act` with the DART expert relabels (`train_actions_expert.npy`)
whenever that file existed, and the SAME overwritten array was then fed to
`rnn_states()`, which replays it into the frozen MDN-RNN's LSTM
(`:99-118`). `train_mdnrnn.py` only ever trains that RNN on executed
actions from `splits.load_proc`, so `h_t` was built from a counterfactual
action sequence that never produced the observed latents `mu` -- worst on
exactly the recovery frames where executed and expert actions differ. This
directly touches the Appendix Z.3 null result ("adding 6.67% recovery data
left val MSE essentially unchanged, 0.001754 -> 0.001788").

**WHY:** `act` has two uses in this file that must NOT share one array. The
LSTM input needs the EXECUTED sequence, because that is what actually
produced `mu` (causality) and what serve time will always have (a deployed
policy only ever knows its own executed history, never an oracle relabel).
The BC loss target needs the EXPERT sequence when DART relabels exist,
because that is what `collect_recovery.py`'s executed actions
(injected noise, "log_expert_steer substituted on noise frames") are
explicitly wrong to clone. Feeding the expert sequence into the LSTM input
too was silently answering the loss target's question with itself on every
recovery frame -- an information leak, not a data-quality problem.

**HOW:**
- [ml/train_controller.py:196-220](../ml/train_controller.py) -- `act` stays
  the executed sequence; a new `act_target` (== `act` when no expert file
  exists, else `np.load(train_actions_expert.npy)`) is introduced. An assert
  pins the two arrays to equal length.
- `:253-254` (the two `rnn_states()` calls) -- unchanged; correct now that
  `act` itself is never overwritten.
- `:258-259` (`fit_a`, `val_a`, the BC loss target) -- switched from `act` to
  `act_target`.
- [ml/diag_copycat.py:85-99](../ml/diag_copycat.py) -- inherited the identical
  bug via the same imported `rnn_states()`. Same split applied, with the
  choice made explicit in a comment: `rnn_states()` gets executed `act`
  (matches what the loaded checkpoint's own `h` was actually trained on, and
  what serve time will always have); `a_t`/`a_prev`/`var` (the copycat
  comparison targets, `:131-132,142`) get `act_target`, since those measure
  the model against what it was trained to hit, not against the noisy
  executed signal it was never trained to match.
- Both files syntax-checked (`ast.parse`) after editing; no other lines
  touched.

**RE-RUN, Appendix Z.3's comparison, with the fixed code:**

Offline (held-out MSE, MLP arch, 3 seeds, `ml/data/proc` vs
`ml/data/proc_aug`, V/M frozen -- same protocol as Z.3/AA):

| arm | pre-fix (existing `cl_base`/`cl_aug` checkpoints) | post-fix (`cl_base_ei`/`cl_aug_ei`, retrained this session) |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (`proc`, no expert file -- code path untouched by the fix) | 0.001768 | 0.001768 (identical, confirms the fix is a no-op here) |
| augmented (`proc_aug`, expert file present) | 0.001806 (+2.2% vs base) | **0.002078 (+17.6% vs base)** |

Baseline reproduces exactly (0.0017536/0.0017644/0.0017850 seeds 0-2, matching
the pre-existing `history_mlp_seed*.json` files bit for bit) because `proc`
has no `train_actions_expert.npy`, so `act_target = act` unconditionally --
the isolation the fix intended.

Closed-loop, PAIRED (`ml/eval_paired.py`, the P6/Appendix AI-AJ trustworthy
harness -- every arm inside one sim launch, so the track-regeneration
confound cancels; Z.3 predates this harness and used the unpaired
`eval_in_sim.py`, so these numbers are a new measurement, not a like-for-like
replication of Z.3's own table). 3 launches x 3 seeds x 1 episode, max 600
steps, real `donkey_sim.exe`:

| arm | steps | mean\|cte\| | ctrl Hz | survived |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| expert (reference) | 600.0 +- 0.0 | 0.363 | 20.00 | 9/9 |
| baseline (`cl_base_ei`) | 155.3 +- 25.7 | 0.707 | 19.96 | 0/9 |
| augmented (`cl_aug_ei`) | 199.0 +- 106.8 | 0.739 | 20.00 | 0/9 |

Paired diff (aug - base), within-launch: mean **+43.7 steps**, sd **110.1**,
n=3 launches, per-launch **[-41.7, +168.0, +4.7]**. The sign flips between
launches and the spread is 2.5x the mean -- not a reliable effect at this n,
the same shape of unreliability Z.3 itself flagged about launch-to-launch
noise.

**DOES Z.3's CONCLUSION SURVIVE?** Yes, and the offline half is now a
sharper negative than before. "No clear improvement from recovery data"
still holds: 0/9 survived in both arms (unchanged), and the paired
closed-loop difference nominally favors the augmented arm but is engulfed by
its own noise at n=3 launches -- not distinguishable from zero. What changed
is the offline metric that Appendix AA used to argue for an escape hatch (the
recovery-weight sweep): pre-fix, held-out MSE made augmented look almost
free (+2.2%); post-fix, with the leak closed, it costs +17.6% MSE for no
measurable closed-loop gain. The pre-fix number was propping up recovery
data's case more than the true signal did -- the counterfactual LSTM input
was letting the model partially answer its own recovery-frame targets during
training, which cannot happen at serve time.

**WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE:** the paired closed-loop n is small (3 launches)
by construction (the mean-driving-time test is expensive; Z.3's own n=9 was
already flagged as marginal). A `--recovery-weight` sweep (Appendix AA) has
not been re-run against the fixed code and might read differently now that
the escape hatch's own MSE justification is gone. Not run here --
out of this task's scope.

untracked). Appendix EI (the audit that found this) and this entry are both
