# Appendix HI - Print-friendly CAD rules research brief (2026-10-12, ~23:18 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan (2026-10-12): /research-brief on making 3D-printer-friendly
CAD files, after servo mount v6's pin holes printed too tight (HH). Brief:
`docs/research/2026-10-12_print-friendly-cad-rules.md`. Desk research; no
print or measurement made.

**Findings (detail, quotes and sources in the brief):**
1. Printed holes come out undersized by a printer + filament + slicer
   specific amount -> calibrate a clearance per fit type. Published PLA data
   (vertical holes): Popescu et al. 2022, 0.12-0.20 mm under for 6-10 mm
   holes at 0.2 mm layers, 0.15-0.36 mm under for 4.5 mm inclined holes;
   Grgic et al. 2023 adopted 0.13 mm slicer hole expansion. The project's own
   two PLA fits (D-bore +0.15 fits; pins +0.075 too tight) are ONE
   confounded source and only consistent with ~+0.15 - the 4.95 holes (HG)
   remain UNTESTED.
2. Bambu Studio's X-Y hole compensation grows hole diameters by 2x the value
   and is calibrated per filament. Evan's current value is UNKNOWN; if it is
   non-zero every fit number in the repo is slicer-dependent. First action.
3. Elephant's foot: P-series setting 0.15 (Bambu release notes); our Lego
   holes have a 6.2 x 0.8 recess at the bed face, so the bore should miss
   the flare - argued, not measured.
4. PLA upright tensile 36% below flat (Eryildiz 2021: 55.49 vs 35.52 MPa):
   keep loads in the layer plane; the camera mast's uprights are the part to
   watch.
5. 13 ranked rules: read and pin the slicer profile; named fit classes in
   lib/lego.scad; print the coupon first (add a 4.90-5.05 pin row);
   vertical pin holes; lead-in chamfers; recess/chamfer bed faces; no
   unsupported overhang below 45 deg; >= 3 perimeters for loaded walls
   (and calibrate with the same wall count - more walls make holes
   smaller); load in-plane; overlap-never-touch meshes; 0.2-0.3 mm static
   clearances; measure bores in the render check; one fixed print profile
   for fit-critical parts.

**Process:** two parallel Sonnet research agents (vendor docs; studies +
OpenSCAD + polyholes); Opus re-read 16 of 18 load-bearing claims at source
(curl, Crossref, PDF text, browser pane for MDPI's table DOM) - all present.
Cold assessment downgraded 4 claims (H1 "survived" -> supported with an
untested rival; project fits -> one confounded source; rival dismissal ->
argued, not measured; chamfer size -> unsourced judgment), added 6
limitations and rule 13, moved the vendor-concentration note to the TL;DR.

**Open:** Evan's Bambu Studio X-Y hole compensation (and the other profile
values) for the PLA prints so far; the PLA fit coupon is still unprinted.

# Appendix HM - Servo bench: lock 450-2600 us, 100-150 us of steering free play (2026-10-13, ~11:19 CDT)
**WHAT (bench measurement, Evan, 2026-10-13):** MG90D-270 on the car,
driven by `firmware/servo_bench` (pulse typed in us):
- **450 us = full lock turning LEFT; 2600 us = full lock turning RIGHT.**
- **Hysteresis / free play:** coming back from full left (450), commanding
  1500 does NOT straighten the wheels; Evan sets **1650 then 1500** and they
  are straight. Coming back from full right (2600), he sets **1400 then
  1500**. So the steering needs an overshoot of 150 us (from the left) and
  100 us (from the right) past centre before 1500 gives straight wheels.
  Evan's reading: "low tolerance in the system" (mechanical play).

**Caveat found in the firmware:** `servo_bench` clamps every pulse to
400-2600 us (US_MIN/US_MAX, `servo.attach(PIN_SERVO, 400, 2600)`). 2600 is
that ceiling, so "full right lock at 2600" may be the bench limit, not the
steering's mechanical lock. 450 sits above the 400 floor, so the left value
is a real reading. Not yet known: whether 450 / 2600 put the steering
against a hard stop (servo straining) or are where the servo itself stops.

**Arithmetic (estimates, not measurements):** at the listing's unverified
0.135 deg/us, 100-150 us of overshoot is 13.5-20 deg of servo rotation taken
up as free play. Through the bare-linkage ratio from 2026-09-05 (58 deg wheel
/ 270 deg pinion, unconfirmed on the current rack) that is roughly 2.9-4.3
deg of wheel angle. The MG90D's own deadband is not this large (typical hobby
servos: a few us; not measured), so the play is most likely in the drive
train: servo spline <-> coupler, coupler <-> Lego axle, pinion <-> rack, tie
rods, or the servo moving in its mount.

**Why it matters:** a steering dead zone of this size means small steering
corrections from a controller produce no wheel motion until the play is
taken up - the classic cause of weaving / limit cycles in lane keeping.

**Firmware state unchanged:** uno_control still has SERVO_US_CENTRE 1500,
SERVO_US_SPAN 450 (+/-450 us) and an unlimited attach(); not reflashed.
**Status:** measured by hand on the bench; free-play location not found.

# Appendix HN - Servo right lock about 2650 us (estimate past the bench ceiling) (2026-10-13, ~11:34 CDT)
**WHAT (Evan, 2026-10-13):** answering the HM caveat - the steering goes "a tiny bit beyond 2600, maybe 2650". So the right-hand lock is about **2650 us**, an ESTIMATE: servo_bench clamps every pulse at 2600 (US_MAX), so nothing above 2600 has been commanded or measured.

**Consequence (arithmetic):** travel from the straight-ahead command (1500, reached after the overshoot of HM) is about 1050 us to the left (450) and about 1150 us to the right (~2650) - not symmetric; the midpoint of the two locks is about 1550 us. Firmware limits must be chosen inside BOTH locks with margin; nothing changed in firmware yet.

**Open:** an exact right-lock value needs servo_bench US_MAX raised (e.g. 2700) and reflashed; whether either lock is a hard mechanical stop (servo straining) is still unknown; the free-play location (HM) is still unknown.

# Appendix HO - Servo right lock = servo end of travel (~2600 us), rack 0.5 mm short of its stop (2026-10-13, ~11:36 CDT)
**WHAT (Evan, 2026-10-13):** servo_bench reflashed with US_MAX 2600 -> 2800 (`firmware/servo_bench/servo_bench.ino:20`, Evan's local edit, uncommitted when this was written). Commanding past 2600 (Evan tried 2700) moves the rack to the SAME angle as 2600, and the rack still has about **0.5 mm** of travel left at that point.

**Conclusion:** the right-hand lock is the SERVO's own end of travel (it stops turning at about 2600 us), not the rack hitting its stop. So on the right the servo cannot stall against the rack. This supersedes HN's "~2650" estimate: pulses above ~2600 add nothing. Right travel from the straight-ahead 1500 is about 1100 us; left (450) about 1050 us.

**Still open:** whether the LEFT lock (450 us) is also the servo's end or the rack's stop (servo straining); where the 100-150 us of free play (HM) lives - the wheel-rocking test.

**Note:** the bench's startup prompt still prints "type us (400-2600)" (servo_bench.ino:36) after the limit change.

# Appendix HP - Left lock is the rack stop; steering slop is the bevel-gear pair (2026-10-13, ~11:39 CDT)
**WHAT (Evan, 2026-10-13):**
1. **Left lock is PHYSICAL**, not the servo: at full left (~450 us) the steering is at its mechanical stop. (Right lock is the servo end of travel, HO.) Consequence: any command past the first-contact point on the left pushes the rack into its stop and STALLS the servo - load on the coupler, the joint never cleared for stall torque (important.md #5). The firmware left limit must sit INSIDE first contact; the first-contact pulse is not yet measured (450 is where Evan saw full lock, not necessarily where contact begins).
2. **The free play (HM, 100-150 us) is located:** the gap between the 2 gears that turn the drive from the servo's axis into the plane of the shaft that drives the rack (the bevel pair before the rack). Gear backlash, not the coupler, not the mount.

**Not yet known:** whether the backlash grows because the two gear axles can spread apart (fixable by holding their spacing) or is the gears' own tooth clearance (needs a preload or removing that gear stage); the gear part numbers / tooth counts.

# Appendix HR - Steering backlash compensation in uno_control (overshoot, then return) (2026-10-13, ~11:46 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan (2026-10-13) chose option D for the steering gear backlash
(HM-HQ) with his own twist: on a move, overshoot past the target, then come
back to the target ("going from 1500 to 2000 make it go to 2060 then back to
2000"). Implemented in `firmware/uno_control/uno_control.ino` (source only;
NOT flashed).

**Model behind the numbers (Opus, fit to Evan's two observations - exactly
determined, UNVERIFIED):** pure gear backlash with a gap b ~ 250 us and the
straight-ahead rack position at 1525. It reproduces both bench procedures:
from the left the servo must reach 1525 + 125 = 1650, from the right
1525 - 125 = 1400 (Evan's 1650 and 1400); the step back to 1500 is smaller
than the gap, so the rack does not move during it. Consequences used here:
- the overshoot must be HALF the gap, **125 us**, not Evan's illustrative 60
  (with 60 a 1500 -> 2000 move would leave the rack ~65 us short);
- with that overshoot, Evan's overshoot-then-return lands the rack exactly
  on the target AND parks the servo mid-gap, so the next move in either
  direction again needs exactly one half-gap - the method is consistent;
- its cost: after the return the teeth are unloaded, so road forces can move
  the wheels within the gap. A switch keeps the classic alternative.

**Code (diff +101 / -6 lines):**
- SERVO_US_CENTRE 1500 -> **1525** (model's straight-ahead).
- New constants: SERVO_BACKLASH_US 125, SERVO_BACKLASH_RETURN true (false =
  overshoot-and-hold), SERVO_DWELL_BASE_MS 20, SERVO_US_PER_MS 4 (listing
  ~0.1 s/60 deg, unverified), SERVO_US_MIN_SAFE 550 (100 us inside the 450
  rack-stop lock; first contact still unmeasured), SERVO_US_MAX_SAFE 2600.
- `struct Backlash` + pure `backlashCommand(b, target, now)`: on a NEW target
  it sets the direction, dwell = 20 ms + (travel + 125)/4 ms, and returns
  target +/- 125 until the dwell ends, then the target (or keeps the
  overshoot if RETURN is false); an unchanged target never restarts it (the
  watchdog path calls it every loop); clamped to the safe limits; the first
  command approaches from below so the start is deterministic.
- `applyOutputs()` takes `now`; both callers pass it; setup()'s first servo
  write goes through the compensator.
- 10 new SELFTEST checks (first-command overshoot, dwell hold, return,
  no restart on an unchanged target, up/down overshoot, dwell formula, both
  safe-limit clamps, full steer + overshoot inside the limits); a millis()
  wrap is straddled on purpose.
- Steering span unchanged (+/-450): commands stay within 950..2100.

**Checks (real output, 2026-10-13 ~11:46 CDT):** first compile FAILED
("'Backlash' was not declared in this scope") - the .ino preprocessor puts
function prototypes above the first function, before a struct declared
later; fixed by declaring the struct with the constants. Second compile:
"Sketch uses 11998 bytes (37%)", "Global variables use 406 bytes (19%)".
SELFTEST was NOT run: it runs on the Uno, which Evan flashes; no host C++
compiler is installed, so the checks were hand-traced only.

**Not changed (named):** the audit finding that steering follows DISARMED
frames (HJ) - the compensator inherits it; uno_control has never been
flashed since servo_bench replaced it (FT).
**Status:** compiled, not flashed, not bench-tested.

impossible as designed; servo_bench was flashed instead.

**Finding - the steering gate blocks every bench steer (a defect of mine,
record HT):** `steerAllowed()` passes only in OUT_DRIVE, and
`outputModeFor()` returns OUT_DRIVE only when `!packInhibit`. With no pack
divider wired, A0 floats, the pack reads FAULT, and `inhibits()` is true
for FAULT (`packguard.h:65`). So on the bench no ARMED frame can ever move the
servo; it holds its boot pulse. SELFTEST 86/86 tests the gate's truth table,
which is correct as written, so it could not show that the bench never
satisfies it. host_test.py has no steer mode either, and adding one would have
commanded a servo that cannot move. Not fixed: the gate is behaving as
specified; the open question is whether steering should share the pack
inhibit (options logged for Evan: steer ignores pack state; a disarmed-only
bench command; a real voltage on the divider).

Also noted: Pi "full left" (steer -100) targets 1075 us and sends 950 with the
overshoot; +100 targets 1975 and sends 2100 (SPAN 450 from centre 1525). The
return to 0 holds 1650 from the left and 1400 from the right.

# Appendix HX - Backlash MEASURED: centre 1525 confirmed, half-gap 75 us (not 125) (2026-10-13 ~14:07 CDT)
**WHAT:** (2026-10-13 ~14:05 CDT) Evan ran the backlash test from record HW by
hand in servo_bench (Serial Monitor, Newline), holding with NO return to 1500.
He reported the hold pulse that made the wheels straight:

| Run | Approach | Straight at |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Pi full left | from 950 | 1600 |
| 2. Pi full right | from 2100 | 1450 |
| 3. Full left lock | from 450 | 1600 |
| 4. Full right lock | from 2600 | 1450 |

**Result:** centre (1600 + 1450) / 2 = **1525, confirmed**; half-gap
(1600 - 1450) / 2 = **75 us, not 125** (gap 150 us). The two swing sizes give
identical holds, so the dead band does not depend on travel or on loading at
the lock. Resolution is whatever step Evan used to find "straight" (not
reported; the values are multiples of 50, so assume about +/-25 us).

**Why the 125 fit (HR) was wrong:** both of Evan's original procedures
(450 -> 1650 -> 1500, 2600 -> 1400 -> 1500) ended with a return to 1500. That
return reverses direction and re-crosses the gap, so the 1650/1400 overshoots
were never the straight-hold values the fit assumed. The earlier "100-150 us"
estimate (HM-HQ) was the right range.

**Firmware:** `SERVO_BACKLASH_US` 125 -> 75 in `uno_control.ino`, comments
updated (centre note + compensator block). SELFTEST checks are written in the
constant; both safe-limit clamp cases still clamp at 75 (560-75 = 485 < 550;
2550+75 = 2625 > 2600). Compiles, 11658 B.

**Flash: FAILED, not on the board.** Upload at 14:06 CDT: "unable to open port
COM3" - the Serial Monitor used for the test still holds the port (tooling.md
trap). The board still runs servo_bench. Re-flash pending Evan closing the
Serial Monitor.

half the collar matches a Lego beam's own counterbore (CB 6.2 x 0.8, record

too small.

# Appendix IF - Pocket gauge: holder snug (0.25/side OK); bank and Pi ~2 mm loose - wrong nominal widths (2026-10-13 ~17:35 CDT)
**WHAT:** (2026-10-13 ~17:35 CDT) Pocket gauge results (PETG print, record
IC). Evan's words: "the largest and middle ones are 2mm loose but the battery
bank has curved edges and i measured from the middle"; then "holder is snug".

| Column | Nominal W used | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Battery bank (widest) | 70.55 | ~2 mm loose |
| Pi 5 Vilros case (middle) | 64.4 | ~2 mm loose |
| 2S holder (narrowest) | 40.5 | snug |

Read as columns (widest = bank, middle = Pi); which of the three U's per
column, and whether "2 mm" is total play or per side, were not stated.

**Reading (Opus):**
- **The "pocket" clearance (0.25 per side) is fine** - the holder, a
  straight-sided part, is snug.
- **The bank's nominal width is wrong for a 4 mm fence**: 70.55 is its width
  at mid-height (Evan measured "from the middle"); its edges are rounded, so
  at the height a 4 mm fence touches it is about 2 mm narrower. The tray's bank
  fence (FENCE_H 4.0) has the same fault: the bank would rattle ~2 mm.
- **The Pi case's 64.4 is likely too big**: ~2 mm loose agrees with the
  vendor's 62.2 width (record FZ: 90.2 x 62.2 x 26.7) rather than Evan's
  earlier 64.4. Rounded edges or a wrong number - not yet known.

**Proposed fix (Opus recommends A, awaiting measurements):** A) raise the
bank fence (and if needed the Pi brackets) past the curve so they hold the
flat side at full width; B) narrow the pockets to the curved bottom (holds
only the curve - the part can tip out). Needs: the height above the bank's
bottom where the curve ends; the Pi case's width at its bottom edge and
whether it is rounded.

# Appendix IJ - Velcro (4 mm) for the bank, holder and Pi - the tie slots could never close; tray v7 / deck v8 (2026-10-13 ~19:05 CDT)
**WHAT:** (2026-10-13 ~19:05 CDT) Retention for the bank, holder and Pi case
switched from zip ties to velcro (Evan: "I'll do velcro so they are
removable ... roughly 4mm").

**Why ties were dropped (a design flaw found 2026-10-13, Opus's own from
GW):** Evan's ties are 100 mm (fit the 3.5 x 1.8 slots) and 200 mm (need slots
about 1.75 x 5.0 by 1.5 x 1.8 = 8.75 x 2.7, his estimate). A tie must close
its loop. The bank and Pi slots only anchor at the edges, and the holder has
no inner-side slot (it sits against the bank fence), so NO tie length could
close a loop around those three; the rails also block a path under the bank.
Estimated loops (head and tail ~25 mm extra; not measured): holder ~135, bank
~190, Pi ~195 mm vs ~175 usable from a 200 mm tie. Only the small-lobe slot
pairs (charger, XT30) work - 100 mm ties fit those. Opus recommended chaining
two 200 mm ties; Evan chose velcro. Velcro under the holder too is Opus's
assumption (its slots fail the same way), stated to Evan.

**Changes (VELCRO = 4.0 constant in both files, Evan's rough number):**
- Tray v7: bank and holder raised 4 mm onto velcro (LAYOUT zones for the
  velcro, parts on top); fences 10 -> 14 mm so the lifted bank's flat band
  (7 mm above its bottom) is still held; posts 42 -> 46 so the fuse holder on
  the lifted bank still clears the deck (2.2 mm). Bank/holder tie slots left
  in place, unused.
- Deck v8: underside 42 -> 46; Pi case on 4 mm velcro, corner brackets 6 ->
  10 mm (else they would hold 2 mm of the case).
- Probes: tray post holes 42.1, bbox z 46, fence/lead-in points +4; deck all
  z +4 (bracket points +8), bbox z 46..58.5.
- docs/ELECTRONICS_LAYOUT.md updated.

# Appendix IP - The 2S holder has no reachable midpoint - the BMS MB wire cannot be made as planned (2026-10-14 ~13:50 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan (2026-10-14): "i cant connect anything in between the 2
batteries". The MB (midpoint) wire planned since 2026-10-10 - "solder to [the
DIANN holder's] strap" (WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md section 2.1, MB row) - cannot be
made on the holder he has. Why it is not possible (strap enclosed, or other) was
not stated.

**Why it matters:** a 2S BMS watches each cell through B+ / MB / B-. Without MB
it cannot see either cell on its own, so the per-cell over-discharge cutoff
(2.9 V) that important.md #4 requires is not provided; boards of this kind may
also read the missing tap as a dead cell and stay off. The firmware pack sense
reads the total only, so a weak cell hides behind a healthy one. Leaving MB
floating is NOT an option.

**Not decided yet** - options given to Evan: two 1S holders in series (the link
wire is the MB tap; a purchase - BLOCKED-ON-EVAN), open the existing holder to
reach its strap, or a printed 2S holder with its own tap (needs contacts not on
hand). Never solder to the cells themselves. Pack wiring is BLOCKED until one is
chosen.

# Appendix IQ - MB tap: the brass rivet on the holder's no-lead end is likely the series node - meter before soldering (2026-10-14 ~13:52 CDT)
**WHAT:** Follow-up to IP. Evan sent a photo of the 2S holder: the end WITHOUT
the leads carries a brass star rivet on its outside face (plus a round hole and
a slot). Inside, the lead end has the + button (red lead) in one slot and a
spring in the other; the rivet end has a spring in one slot and the other
slot's contact behind the rivet. In a 2-cell series holder the end without the
leads is where cell 1 - meets cell 2 +, so the rivet is most likely the series
node = MB. This is an inference from the photo, NOT yet metered.

**Plan (unblocks IP if the meter agrees):** cells in, meter rivet -> black lead
and rivet -> red lead; both must read 3.6-4.2 V (one cell each). If they do:
cells OUT, scrape / tin the rivet, solder the MB wire quickly (the plastic holds
the contact - long heat can loosen it), sleeve it. With the BMS on the holder
top (IO), MB now runs from the end opposite the leads - so place the BMS MB pad
toward that end; MB stays short (~20-40 mm estimate).

**Changed:** WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md section 2.1 MB row notes the rivet and the
meter gate. Option 1 of IP (two 1S holders) is not needed if the meter passes.

# Appendix IY - First charge: charger was wired reversed; swapped, now charging (CR LED) (2026-10-15 ~12:52 CDT)
**WHAT:** First charge attempt, charger (Adeept p0374) and XT30 now on the BMS
P+ / P- pads (IW). Symptom: green "OK" LED on, pack voltage did not rise in
15 min; XT30 read -8.80 V with USB-C in; at the fuse holder (cell side) 7.11 V.
Evan had already fitted a NEW 9 V battery in the DT830B (so these readings are
not the low-battery suspicion raised in IR).

**Root cause (found by Evan):** the charger was wired REVERSED - red to the
charger's GND, black to BAT. Evan swapped the two wires; the red "CR" LED is now
lit (charging). No heat, smoke or damage reported. Consistent with the BMS
switching off its output against a reversed charger (cell side stayed 7.11 V
while the P side followed the charger, 8.8 V the other way round). The
charger's own output voltage is still unknown: 8.80 V was read against a
nearly open circuit and may be its no-battery float, not its charge voltage.

**Gate on this charge:** watch the pack voltage at the end - it must stop at or
below ~8.4 V (4.2 V per cell); above 8.45 V means the charger overcharges -
unplug and do not use it. Then rest 30 min and meter each cell (rivet to each
lead) for balance. Whether the reversed hookup stressed the BMS or charger is
not known; their protection functions remain UNTESTED.

# Appendix IZ - First charge stopped early at 3.83 V per cell (not overcharged); charger reads ~8.8 V with no load (2026-10-15 ~14:12 CDT)
**WHAT:** First charge result (continues IY). Readings by Evan, DT830B with the
new 9 V battery:
- 15 min: cells (fuse side) 7.50 V, XT30 7.75 V (0.25 V across BMS + fuse +
  wire under charge current).
- +25 min: cells 7.82 V, XT30 8.09 V; charger board "a little hot", holdable
  for an extended time; nothing else warm.
- Charger then went to green "OK". Still plugged in: pack and XT30 both
  jumping 8.75-8.92 V. Told to unplug at once (above 8.4 V for 2S).
- Unplugged and rested: each cell 3.83 V (both equal - balanced), P+ to P-
  7.68 V.

**Reading:** the cells were NOT overcharged - they rest at 3.83 V each, well
under 4.2 V - and the charge stopped early (~3.83 V/cell at rest is roughly
half to two-thirds full; a full 25R rests ~4.1-4.2 V). WHY it stopped early is
NOT known. Candidates, none tested: the charger terminates on its own terminal
voltage, which the 0.25-0.27 V path drop pushes up; or the BMS cut the charge
path and the charger then floated to its no-load ~8.8 V (also seen in IY). The
8.75-8.92 V plugged-in reading is therefore most likely the charger's no-load
output, not the cells.

**Open:** the charger's real no-load output (BAT lifted, USB-C in, BAT to GND)
- 8.4 V is correct; a steady 8.8 V means the board is wrong for this pack.
Until measured: no further charging.

**WHAT:** Evan confirmed the charger board swap (JC) happened BEFORE the second

# Appendix JE - Build step 1: LM2596 set to 4.95 V unloaded (meter), display 4.9 (2026-10-15 ~17:50 CDT)
**WHAT:** WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md section 5 step 1 done by Evan: LM2596 (EPLZON,
with display) fed from the charged pack (8.29 V after JA) through an XT30-female
bench lead, output UNLOADED, set to **4.95 V on the DT830B** (the module's own

Whether the trim pot was locked was not stated.

# Appendix JF - Uno powered by the Pi's USB, not the LM2596 - no cut cable; servo moves to +5V2 (2026-10-16 ~13:02 CDT)
**WHAT:** Power-entry change, Evan's decision (option 1). Before wiring step
1b, Evan asked why the Uno could not run from the power bank's own port. The
bank's USB-A cannot: the Uno has one USB jack and it carries the Pi link. But
the idea exposed a simpler design: the Pi is already on the bank, so the Pi's
USB cable can power the Uno. The "Uno 5V pin fed from the LM2596 through a
cut-5V cable" architecture was stated as a rule in record CR with no reason
beyond avoiding two supplies back-feeding - which this also avoids, as long as
the LM2596 never touches the Uno's 5V pin.

**New design:** Pi 5 USB-A -> Uno over a PLAIN USB cable (power + data). The
LM2596 (`+5V2`, 4.99 V, JE) feeds only the servo V+, both strip segments and
the encoder Vcc. TB6612 VCC (logic) stays on the Uno 5V pin, now USB 5 V. One
shared ground at the star; the USB cable's ground is the single Pi-to-star
connection (bank and pack are separate batteries, so no loop).

**Why (vs the cut cable):** no cable surgery; the old step 1b risk (the clone's
FT232RL possibly needing USB 5 V) is gone; and the Uno now survives a dead pack,
blown fuse, tripped BMS or rocker OFF - A0 reads ~0 V -> PACK_FAULT, which
inhibits driving AND is reported, where before the Uno simply went dark (the
2026-10-11 audit's "FAULT is never seen"). A slowly dying pack crosses CUTOFF
(latched until reset) before the BMS trips. Checked against
firmware/uno_control/packguard.h (FAULT below 4000 mV, inhibits()): no
firmware change needed.

**Costs:** rocker OFF no longer powers the Uno down; its output pins can push a
little current into the unpowered strips / servo / encoder - the strips already
have 400 ohm DIN resistors (shield item 5); servo and encoder back-feed is
unmeasured. **Evan's follow-up question - "isn't the servo on the Arduino's 5V"
- matters:** on the bench (servo_bench, HM-HX) the servo was powered from the
Uno; in the car it MUST be on `+5V2`, never the Uno's 5V header: stall current
through the Uno's USB polyfuse and the Pi port would brown the Uno out.

**Edited:** WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md - power diagram (Pi USB -> Uno), `+5V2` row,
a superseded-note over the three old warnings (kept as history), pack-sense
FAULT note, build steps 1b (plain-cable host_test) and 3 (flash over the normal
cable); BOM row 20 (cable no longer cut). Not edited: the old warnings' text
(history). Untested on hardware.

# Appendix JG - Barrel-jack idea for the Uno: the bank can give 12 V only if the cable negotiates it; test given (2026-10-16 ~13:44 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan proposed powering the Uno from the power bank's USB-A port via
an A -> C adapter and his USB-C -> barrel-jack cable. Claude first said the
USB-A port gives only 5 V - **wrong as stated**: Evan read the bank's label,
which rates the output up to 12 V. Corrected: the higher voltage needs the
cable to NEGOTIATE it (Quick Charge on USB-A; USB-PD on USB-C); a plain or
PD-only barrel cable gets 5 V through USB-A, and the Uno barrel jack needs
7-12 V (onboard regulator dropout ~1-1.2 V; 5 V in leaves ~3.8-4 V).

**Test given (free, not yet run):** meter the barrel plug from the bank's USB-C
port, then through the A -> C adapter on USB-A; 9-12 V on the second = the
idea works electrically. Claude's view: not worth adding even then - the Pi
USB cable (needed for data) already powers the Uno under JF; the barrel saves
~50 mA and adds an adapter purchase (Evan's go), a third cable and a
re-negotiation fallback. Evan wants to try it; JF stays the plan of record.

**Next (Evan):** Raspberry Pi 5 set-up (PRD task 9's Pi half: OS, SSH, camera).

# Appendix JN - Servo on the Uno's 5V via Pi USB: no reset seen, one garbled line; bank was flaky (2026-10-16 ~17:12 CDT)
**WHAT:** Servo-supply test (JF question), servo on the Uno's 5V header, Uno
on the Pi 5's USB, Pi on the power bank, `servo_bench` on the board, driven
from the Pi with `python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm /dev/ttyUSB0 115200`.

**Run 1:** 1500 (boot), 1525, 2400, 600, then `c` (centre, Evan) -> 1500,
1525. No banner reprint = no reset. No stall hold was done.
**Run 2:** 1500 (boot), 1525, **400** (past the ~450 us left rack stop - a
stall against the stop; hold time not stated), 1525, **2600** (servo end),
then a line printed as **`->150 us`** (malformed: the firmware prints
`-> NNNN us`; Evan's input there not stated - likely `c` / 1500 with two
characters lost), 1525. No banner reprint in either run = **no Uno reset
seen**.

**Reading (not conclusive):** the Uno survived a stall at 400 us and full
lock-to-lock swings on Pi-USB power - evidence FOR Evan's servo-on-Uno-5V
preference. But the malformed line right after the 2600 -> centre swing is a
possible serial glitch from supply noise; it is unexplained. `dmesg` was not
captured. Evan then reported the bank was "flakey" and is switching to a newer
bank - so this run's supply was itself suspect.

**To close it:** repeat on the new bank: 450 hold ~3 s x3, full swings, then
`dmesg | grep -i -E "over-current|usb"`; count malformed lines. Then re-flash
uno_control and re-run host_test (the real step 1b gate, JM).

# Appendix JO - Servo test: run 2 was on the new bank; the garbled line was a lost-byte glitch on c; no USB over-current (2026-10-16 ~17:13 CDT)
**WHAT:** Clarifications and dmesg for the servo-supply test (corrects JN):
- Run 2 (400 / 2600 / garbled line) was on the NEW power bank, not the flaky
  one - JN called that run's supply "suspect"; that was wrong. Run 1 was on
  the old, flaky bank.
- The garbled `->150 us` line WAS Evan pressing `c`. servo_bench prints
  `-> 1500 us` for `c` (servo_bench.ino:30, :43; run 1 printed it correctly),
  so TWO characters were lost on the Uno -> Pi serial line, right after the
  2600 -> 1500 swing - the largest servo move of the run.
- `dmesg | grep -i -E "over-current|usb"`: no over-current; the FT232R
  (0403:6001, ttyUSB0) attached once at boot (~5.6 s) and never
  disconnected/re-enumerated. ("Unable to read latency timer: -32" at attach -
  common on FT232 clones, not investigated.)

**Reading:** on Pi-USB power the servo on the Uno's 5V did NOT reset the Uno
and did NOT trip the Pi's USB port, but a large servo move corrupted serial
data (2 bytes lost). Most likely cause: servo current surges disturbing the
shared 5 V that also powers the Uno's FT232 / UART (not proven). In
uno_control every frame is CRC-checked, so corruption becomes dropped frames;
bursts during steering could approach the 150 ms watchdog. One event, not a
rate.

**Options given to Evan:** servo + on `+5V2` (recommended; the 3-pin jumper
keeps the swap one move), or keep the Uno 5V and add a 470 uF cap at the servo
header, then measure the CRC_BAD rate with uno_control while steering.

# Appendix JP - Servo on the Uno's 5V: serial bytes lost on 2 of 3 big swings, 0 of 16 at rest (2026-10-16 ~17:15 CDT)
**WHAT:** Run 3 of the servo-supply test (new bank; servo on the Uno's 5V;
Uno on the Pi's USB; servo_bench via miniterm on the Pi). 25 reply lines:
- 16 x `-> 1500 us` with the servo AT REST (repeated `c`): all clean.
- 400, then 2600, then `c` -> printed **`-> 1500 u`** (one character lost),
  then two clean 1500s, 2600, 1500 (clean), 400, 1500 (clean).

**Tally across runs 2 and 3 (JN, JO):** every corrupted line (2 of them)
came on the reply to a LARGE move, 2600 -> 1500, the moment the servo starts
its biggest swing; 0 corrupted of 16 replies at rest; large swings to centre
were corrupted in 2 of 3 cases (2600 -> 1500), 0 of 2 for 400 -> 1500. No
resets, no USB disconnects (dmesg, JO).

**Reading:** a reproducible correlation, not a one-off: serial bytes from the
Uno are lost when the servo draws its start-of-swing surge from the same 5 V
(Uno 5V header <- Pi USB). Mechanism (supply ripple reaching the FT232 / UART)
is likely, not measured - no scope. In uno_control this becomes CRC-rejected
frames exactly when steering changes fastest. Small sample (n = 3 large swings
to centre).

**Recommendation stands, now on data:** servo + on `+5V2` (LM2596), with the
3-pin jumper on the shield; optionally also a 470 uF cap at the servo header.
Evan's call. Then re-flash uno_control and run host_test on the Pi.

# Appendix JR - Decision: the servo runs from the Uno's 5V header (Evan); jumper to +5V2 kept as the fallback (2026-10-16 ~17:24 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan's decision: the steering servo is powered from the Uno's 5V
header (USB 5 V from the Pi), not from `+5V2`. Reason (Evan): ease of setup and
repair - three pins into the shield on the Uno - and it has worked: drove the
rack incl. the left stop on PC USB (HM-HQ), and on Pi USB with no Uno reset and
no USB over-current (JN, JO).

**Against (Claude's recommendation, rejected):** `+5V2` + a 3-pin jumper.
Data JP: with the servo on the Uno 5V, 2 of 3 large swings (2600 -> 1500 us)
lost serial bytes Uno -> Pi; 0 of 16 replies at rest. In uno_control a
corrupted frame is CRC-rejected, so the cost is dropped steering updates during
the fastest steering changes - unmeasured as a rate.

**Mitigation kept:** fit the 3-pin jumper on the shield (Uno 5V | servo + |
`+5V2`); re-measure the CRC_BAD rate while steering lock to lock once the pack
is wired to the shield; optional 470 uF at the servo header.

**Edited:** WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md (servo table V+, `+5V2` row, power diagram,
the JF rules line); decisions.md; HANDOFF state line.

# Appendix JS - Pack-side wiring diagram (docs/pack_wiring_full.svg); LM2596 stays 5.0 V; motor hookup (2026-10-16 ~17:58 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan asked (1) what the LM2596 should be set to now that only the
motor side and lights run from the pack, (2) where exactly the motor wires in,
and (3) for an SVG of everything connected to the 18650 pack.

**Answers (no design change):**
- LM2596 stays at **5.0 V** (4.99 V is right): the WS2812B strips are 5 V
  parts, and the encoder's Vcc comes from `+5V2` while its A / B outputs swing
  to that Vcc into Uno D2 / D3 - so `+5V2` must sit level with the Uno's own
  5 V (now the Pi's USB, which can sag toward ~4.8 V under servo load). The
  motor is not on the buck: VBAT -> TB6612 VM, speed by PWM.
- Motor: the 6-wire JST cable - red / black to TB6612 AO1+BO1 / AO2+BO2
  (bridged), blue -> `+5V2`, green -> star, yellow -> D2, white -> D3; TB6612
  VM <- VBAT, GND pad = the star, VCC <- Uno 5V, D11 / D8 / D12 / D10 for
  PWM / direction / STBY; 470-1000 uF at VM, 0.1 uF across the motor. The
  channel pairing is still flagged unverified against the datasheet
  (WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md 2.2).

**New file:** `docs/pack_wiring_full.svg` - pack -> XT30 -> rocker -> VBAT ->
TB6612 / LM2596 / divider, motor + encoder, strips; Uno pins as net labels;
every ground symbol = its own wire to the star; Uno and servo marked as NOT on
the pack (JF, JR). Linked at the top of WIRING_PROTOSHIELD.md section 2.0;
the tables stay the authority. Drawn from the section 2 tables, not from the
built hardware (step 2b onward is unbuilt).

# Appendix KB - Deck v13: LM2596 was flush against a Lego-pin boss (Evan caught it); checker now fails parts touching material at a side (2026-10-20 ~17:57 CDT)
**WHAT:** Evan (2026-10-20): "the hole for the lego connectors interfere with
the buck converter". He is right; the layout checker missed it.

**Symptom -> root cause -> fix:**
- Symptom: in deck v12 (JW) the LM2596 box (x 10..76, y -78..-42, from z 60)
  sat flush against the -y lobe boss at (60, -82) (8 x 8, y -86..-78, z
  54.5..62.3). The boss rises 2.3 mm above the board's underside, with 0 mm
  side gap. JW's wing re-order moved the board from x 62..128 (which only
  grazed that boss) onto it.
- Root cause: `electronics_layout.py` check (a) samples only INSIDE each box
  (inset 0.3) and check (b) treats a shared face as no overlap. So a part
  pressed flush against a raised printed feature passed.
- Fix (checker): parts (not zones or clearances) now also fail if material is
  within `SIDE_CLEAR` = 0.2 mm outside any side face. Pockets give 0.25, so
  the fenced bank, holder and Pi still pass. Run on deck v12, it failed only
  the LM2596: "material inside or within 0.2 mm of a side at (59.35, -78.20,
  60.30)". No other part flagged. Self-check (a2): a part flush against a tray
  post is caught.
- Fix (deck v13): LM2596 +4 in y, so y -74..-38 with a 4 mm gap to the boss.
  Pegs `LM_XY` y -44.25 / -75.75 -> -40.25 / -71.75; terminal zones follow.
  The probe for the peg moved with it.

**Checks (real output, 2026-10-20 ~17:56 CDT):** deck render 97/97 probes,
manifold; layout 35 entries, 0 checks failed; self-check PASS incl. (a2);
check_artifacts 40, 0 drifted; run_checks 17 passed. Not committed.

**Lesson:** "0 checks failed" said nothing about contact, only about overlap.
Every new check type should be run once against a known-bad case first.
